V12/AboutModal.title: About modal
V12/AboutModal.summary:
A small passive modal that says what a product is and which version runs. It
shows a logo over the title, the content, a row of links, additional information
and a copyright line. One additional information item shows as a block; several
show as tabs. It follows `open` and closes itself unless `onClose` returns
`false`. The close button, Escape or a press outside closes it, and focus goes
back to the launcher.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **The modal's snap:** the overlay fades in, and the surface arrives centred
  from 92% of its box, leaning toward what opened it. Leaving, it pulls back.
  `backdrop` and `shadow` are the modal's.
- **Content:** the body moves in with the frame, as in the modal.
- **Tabs:** with several additional information items, the marker glides between
  tabs, and the panels swap out, then in. `timeScale` reaches the tabs too.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The modal's: the overlay and the surface only fade, at their final geometry, on
half the clock. The tabs' selector fades on the new tab on half the clock, and
the panels swap at once.

V12/Accordion.title: Accordion
V12/Accordion.summary:
Headings that open and shut the content under them. `Accordion` holds the items.
`AccordionItem` is a heading button with a chevron, over the body it opens.
`AccordionSkeleton` is the accordion while it loads. They take Carbon's props,
plus `exclusive`, `headingLevel`, `corners`, `frame` and `timeScale`. An item's
`open` is its initial state, and it is followed whenever it changes; a click
toggles it in between. Enter or Space toggles an item; ↑, ↓, Home and End move
between the headings.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
The body is the shared disclosure.

- **Body:** the height travels on the step for its travel: under 24px fast-02,
  under 120px moderate-01, under 480px moderate-02, under 900px moderate-03,
  else slow-01. Opening is on entrance-productive. Shutting is one step faster,
  on exit-productive.
- **One motion:** every body that changes in one commit moves on one clock, the
  step of the farthest travel. Expand all and collapse all are one motion. With
  more than one body, the step is never slower than moderate-02, before a shut's
  step down. With `exclusive`, opening one item shuts the other, as one swap on
  standard-productive.
- **Soft edge:** while it moves, the clip's bottom fades over
  `min(16px, h, H − h)`, so it is gone on the frame the body lands.
- **Content in:** the content waits 8px above and comes down into place from the
  opening's first frame, over one duration token longer than the body. It
  settles last.
- **Content out:** the content holds still while the edge closes over it.
- **Turn:** a change mid-move starts from the body's live height and takes the
  step of what is left.
- **Chevron:** down when shut, up when open. The heading is its motion icon
  frame.
- **Rollover:** the kit's rollover on the heading, an even wash across the row.
  It is flush: the row never grows past its hairlines or shrinks from them.
- **First paint:** no motion. Under `exclusive`, the last open item stays open.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
A body opens or shuts at once, with no soft edge. The content fades in on the
reduced clock. The chevron and the hover change at once.

V12/ActivityFeed.title: ActivityFeed
V12/ActivityFeed.summary:
Events in time order, newest first, grouped by day. Each day has a sticky header
that never folds. An event is an avatar with initials, who did what, a status,
its time and an optional detail behind Show details. An event that asks for an
answer can have up to two actions, drawn as small ghost buttons. Today's times
are relative; an earlier day shows the clock time. `categories` adds filter tags
over the list. While `loading`, skeleton rows stand in for the events. With
none, the feed shows an empty state. Give the feed a height: it scrolls inside
it.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **List arrival:** with the reader at the top, a new event's place opens from
  nothing on the step for its height, on entrance-productive. What is below
  follows. Its content comes down 8px into the place. A new day's place opens
  with its header.
- **Place hold:** with the reader further down, nothing in view moves. The row
  being read holds its place as events arrive above it, and Jump to latest shows
  with a count of the new events.
- **Floating snap:** Jump to latest is the kit's JumpTo, set to the top. The
  pill arrives and leaves on its own clock. A jump glides to the top on a clock
  set by the distance.
- **Disclosure:** Show details opens an event's detail with the kit's
  disclosure. The body opens on the step for its travel, and the content moves
  with the opening.
- **Content swap:** a filter change swaps the list out, then in. The events and
  day titles leave 8px up on fast-01, exit-productive. The new ones come in from
  8px below on fast-02, entrance-productive. The top day title holds still when
  its day leads both lists. The view goes back to the top.
- **Soft edge:** under a stuck day title, a divider and a soft edge grow over
  the first 16px of scroll under it, so neither pops.
- **Skeleton reveal:** when the events land, the skeleton dissolves in place as
  they fade in.
- **Stillness:** as a minute passes, a time's words change in place. Only the
  times whose words change render again, never a row or the feed.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
A new event's place is there at once, and its content fades in on the reduced
clock. A filter change swaps the list at once. A detail opens at once, its
content fading in. Jump to latest lands at once, with no glide.

V12/AppShell.title: App shell
V12/AppShell.summary:
The frame an app sits in: a header, a nav, the page, and an optional side panel.
`AppShell` takes the header, the nav (a SideNav) and a `panel`; the page is its
children.

The shell sizes itself from its own width, not the window's:

| Size class | Width          | Nav                           | Panel            |
| ---------- | -------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------- |
| Compact    | under 672px    | overlay, from the menu button | full-width sheet |
| Medium     | 672 to 1055px  | rail of icons                 | covers the page  |
| Expanded   | 1056 to 1311px | column                        | pushes the page  |
| Large      | 1312px and up  | column                        | pushes the page  |

- `scope="page"` fixes the header and scrolls the page with the window;
  `scope="container"` fills its container.
- `frame="inset"` puts the page on a rounded workspace, and
  `headerPlacement="nav"` puts the header at the top of the nav column.
- The header and nav are ghost by default, on chrome that is dark in every theme
  (`chromeTheme`). The page follows the theme; `mainTheme` gives it one of its
  own, and `inverse` is the opposite of the theme's.
- `Header` is the 48px global header, `NavOverlay` the overlay nav alone, and
  `Region` one area of a screen, with its surface, corners and scroll.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
Most of the motion is the parts' own: the rail's fold is the SideNav's, and the
overlay nav and the panel move as side panels.

- **Fold:** with `foldTo="hide"`, the column's width moves to a 56px strip and
  back in one motion, and main follows its edge. The content holds its open
  width while the edge passes over it, and the strip swaps in when it lands. The
  clock is the step for the width's travel, on entrance-productive; shrinking,
  one step faster, on exit-productive. Pressed mid-fold, it turns round from the
  width drawn. The strip is the toggle with an equal inset either side, up to
  the workspace; `foldToggle="header"` puts the toggle at the column's top,
  above what the strip shows. The column carries the fold's progress as
  `--cds-nav-fold`, 0 open to 1 folded, on the same clock, so what is in it can
  move with the fold. `foldTo="overlay"` folds the column away and opens the nav
  from the menu button.
- **Overlay nav:** at compact, the nav is a SidePanel at the start, under the
  header. It snaps in timed by its width, leaves a step shorter, and its content
  rides the opening. The dim fades on the side panel's overlay clocks.
- **Panel push:** at expanded and large, the panel is SidePanel's `slideIn`:
  main makes room on the panel's clock.
- **Class edge:** crossing a size class edge while the panel is open re-places
  it at once. It is the same panel, with no second entrance, its content and
  focus kept. Main's room is given or taken at once.
- **Menu button:** while the overlay is open, the header's menu button is its
  Close. The Menu icon match-cuts to Close, and the button's name changes with
  it.
- **Home link:** the product name has the family's rollover, a glow inset 4px
  from the bar.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The hide fold moves at once. The overlay nav and its dim fade on the reduced
clock. Main makes room for the panel at once. The menu icon changes at once. A
class edge is at once either way.

V12/Breadcrumb.title: Breadcrumb
V12/Breadcrumb.summary:
A trail of links to the levels above the current page. A `nav` holds an ordered
list of `BreadcrumbItem`s. Each one is a link, plain text, an app's own link
element, or an `OverflowMenu` for collapsed levels. The current page is primary
text, marked `aria-current`. In a narrow container the crumbs wrap; each crumb
stays on one line.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Rollover:** each link crumb takes the link rollover: a glow in the letters,
  the press and the release circle. The underline fades in on hover. The current
  page and plain text take no rollover.
- **Overflow menu:** a crumb holding an `OverflowMenu` shows the horizontal
  overflow icon at the breadcrumb's size. Its menu opens on the Menu's snap,
  floating: md, or sm in an sm breadcrumb.
- **Trail:** a change to the trail reflows as one change. A crumb that leaves
  fades out first, over fast-01. Then the crumbs that stay slide to their new
  places, timed by travel. Then a new crumb snaps in, with no fade, sliding from
  the trail's side. Keyed children reflow by key.
- **Removal:** a trail that only loses crumbs plays together: the crumb fades
  out as the others close the gap.
- **Slash:** with `noTrailingSlash`, the last crumb's slash fades out and keeps
  its place, so nothing jumps. A crumb that stops being last fades its slash in.
- **Interruption:** a new change mid-reflow turns round from where the crumbs
  are on screen.
- **Slow motion:** `timeScale` multiplies the reflow's durations. An overflow
  menu takes it too.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Nothing slides. A crumb that leaves fades out on the reduced clock, then the new
places and the new crumbs appear at once. A slash fades in on the reduced clock.
The overflow menu opens and closes at once.

V12/Button.title: Button
V12/Button.summary:
An action's trigger, with Carbon's Button props. `kind` is the role: primary,
secondary or danger. `variant` is the treatment: filled, outlined or tonal.
`frame` is what it stands on: inset, ghost, or none for a text button; it wins
over `variant`. Buttons are pills by default. `busy` shows a spinner in the
icon's place while an action runs. The package also exports `ButtonSet`,
`ButtonSkeleton` and `ButtonGrid`, a set of equal actions in one shell with one
Tab stop.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Hover:** a glow of the matched-lightness hover color under the pointer, in
  on fast-02 and out on fast-01.
- **Size:** the button grows 1px on hover and presses 1px in from its rest edge.
- **Press and release:** the flat pressed color while held. On release, the
  pressed color recedes from the release point as a soft circle. A press dragged
  off the button is cancelled; dragged back on, still held, it presses again.
- **Toned steps:** outlined and ghost buttons hover and press in tints of their
  own color. The label takes one Carbon step further from the backdrop, and more
  if it would fall under 4.5:1.
- **Icon:** a motion icon plays on the button's hover or keyboard focus.
- **Busy:** out, then in. The icon fades out, then the spinner draws on
  (moderate-01). When busy ends, the spinner closes (fast-02), then the icon
  fades back. With no icon, the label takes the icon's turn. An icon with its
  own pending motion, such as Save or Send, keeps it, with no spinner.
- **Focus:** keyboard only. A 2px ring in the button's own text color just
  inside its edge, with a 2px rim of the fill round it on a filled button.
- **ButtonGrid:** each cell has the Button's hover, press and release circle,
  clipped to the cell, with no growth or press-in.
- **ButtonSkeleton:** it pulses on the page's skeleton wave.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The glow, the 1px growth and the press still show, at once. The release circle
and a toned label's step land at once. A motion icon is a still drawing and does
not play. Busy swaps at once, and the spinner is its still dots.

V12/Card.title: Card
V12/Card.summary:
A tile with a header, a body, actions and a footer, on `--cds-surface` with 8px
corners and 16px in. A card has a label, a title and a description, a body,
action icons and an overflow menu, and primary and secondary buttons. With
`onClick` it is a control, one tab stop; without it, it is a plain surface.
`ProductiveCard` is dense, for product UI, with its actions at the top and a
ghost primary button. Its `clickZone` sets where a click counts.
`ExpressiveCard` holds media to the card's edge, or a pictogram, with its
actions at the bottom. `CardSkeleton` is a card while it loads. `decorator` and
`slug` are accepted and render nothing.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Rollover, text card:** a clickable card takes the tiles' quiet rollover,
  painted behind the content, never over it. The surface grows 1px on hover and
  presses 1px in. `hoverSteps="standard"` uses the house steps.
- **Rollover, card with controls:** a clickable card that holds controls hovers
  with a ring.
- **Controls inside:** when a control in the card is hovered or pressed, the
  card yields and its cast shadow steps back. The controls never take the card's
  colors, and a click on one never clicks the card. Outside the click zone, a
  click does nothing and the hover goes back to rest.
- **Cast shadow:** off by default; `shadow` turns it on for a clickable card. It
  is lit from the pointer: the offset follows at once, and the strength fades on
  moderate-01. A press draws it in.
- **Snap:** the overflow menu opens and closes with the kit's menu.
- **Motion icons:** the action icons, the overflow trigger and the button icons
  are motion icons, played by their own buttons.
- `timeScale` multiplies the durations of the rollover, the buttons and the
  overflow menu.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text: The rollover changes at once. The cast shadow's strength changes at once.

V12/Chat.title: Chat shell
V12/Chat.summary:
A chat with an assistant: the conversation, the prompt below it, and what docks
round the prompt. Use it as a page of its own, or in a pane beside a page.

- `ChatShell` holds the header, the conversation and the prompt. It sets the
  look of the parts inside (`variant`, `corners`) and caps them at a reading
  width (`column`).
- `ChatTranscript` is the conversation: the turns, and for each reply the line
  that says what it's doing and the steps it took.
- `PromptInput` is the prompt: a field that grows, its footer controls, Stop,
  attachments and a notice.
- `ChatDock` puts a follow-up question (`FollowUpCard`) above the prompt and
  suggestions (`Suggestions`) below it.
- `ChatTurnNavigator` lists the questions in a long chat and scrolls to the one
  you choose.
- `ChatPane` opens the chat beside a page.
- `ChatMessage`, `TurnStatus`, `StepList` and `FileChips` are the smaller parts,
  for building your own.

sections.title: Working together
sections.text:
- **One thing works at a time.** While a reply is coming, only one part shows
  it: the status line, a running step, the streaming words, or a ring on Stop
  when the reply is out of sight. Each part does this only when asked
  (TurnStatus `working`, StepList `workingStep`, PromptInput `stopRing`);
  ChatTranscript sets the first two and reports `onReplyInView`.
- **The question list.** In the header, ChatTurnNavigator reads the shell's
  conversation. Each question shows its first line and its time, and the marker
  is on the one in view. Alt with ↑ or ↓ steps between questions while focus is
  in the conversation, not on a control.
- **Custom parts.** `useChatVariant` gives a part of your own the shell's
  `variant`.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Content swap in a layout move:** in ChatDock's slots, what leaves plays the
  swap's out toward the prompt (fast-02, exit-productive, 16px). Then every
  changing slot resizes on one clock by the larger travel, standard-productive.
  Then what arrives plays the swap's in (moderate-01, entrance-productive).
- **Arrival:** new turns slide the column up by what they push it, by travel,
  standard-productive. A person's turn fades up in place (fast-02).
- **Pinned scroll:** a reader at the bottom stays there; one who scrolled up is
  never moved.
- **Streaming:** a reply's first words rise 4px as they land (fast-02,
  entrance-productive); then each sentence fades up in place.
- **History:** replies done as the conversation mounts are there, still: no
  stream and no wait for the summary.
- **Send to Stop:** the arrow swaps out, then the square in. The Spinner turns
  round it only while the reply is out of sight.
- **Width move:** ChatPane's width moves by travel on standard-expressive, one
  step faster shutting, its content under the 16px soft edge.
- **Sideways opening:** a file chip opens its space by travel,
  entrance-productive, its content moving with the opening under a soft edge.
- **Status:** dictation's status is a Popover over the prompt in the opposite
  theme, snapping from its edge above the microphone and folding back into it.
- **Rise:** the docked notice rises from behind the field by travel. Its content
  swaps in place; it sinks one step faster.
- **Jump to a question:** the navigator's popover snaps from its button. A
  choice closes it, then the conversation glides to the question and focuses it;
  a wash fades in (fast-02) and out (slow-01).
- **Marker:** in the navigator's list, on the turn in view, moving in place as
  the reader scrolls; never a glide.
- **Selection:** in Suggestions and FollowUpCard, the selector grows in from the
  row's center (fast-02), then the choice is handed on.
- **Status row:** the mark loads in at once and the row comes in through the
  shimmer's band. Each stage's words hold at least one loading period, then
  swap: out, then in through the band. The summary is out, then in.
- **Steps:** a new step's space opens by travel, its content coming from 8px
  back. Queued to running, the dashed circle winds up into the spinner; done,
  the spinner hands off to the status mark in place.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
No travel: fades on the reduced clock, moves landing at once. The outs are at
once, so the working element passes at once, and the first words have no rise. A
jump to a question has no wash. Popovers and panes follow their own reduced
rules. The status row's mark is still and its words plain; its swaps are on the
reduced clock and its details open at once. Steps and their marks land at once,
and their words swap on the reduced clock.

V12/ChatInput.title: ChatInput
V12/ChatInput.summary:
> **Problem statement:** a conversation needs one place to write the next turn:
> a prompt that grows as it is written, the files attached to it, what the model
> may read, which model and mode answer, and a send that becomes Stop while a
> reply is generating. Carbon's `TextArea` is a form field, with a label above
> and no actions. `@carbon/ai-chat` has an input, but it is part of a whole chat
> application and cannot be used on its own. ChatInput is the composer alone,
> standalone React built from Carbon's `Menu`, `Theme` and icons, labs
> `MegaButton` for every control and labs `FileChip` for each attachment.

Its nearest Carbon neighbours are `TextArea` and the input in `@carbon/ai-chat`.
Use `TextArea` for a form field; use `@carbon/ai-chat` for a whole chat
application.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text:

> a prompt that grows as it is written, the files attached to it, what the model
> may read, which model and mode answer, and a send that becomes Stop while a
> reply is generating. Carbon's `TextArea` is a form field, with a label above
> and no actions. `@carbon/ai-chat` has an input, but it is part of a whole chat
> application and cannot be used on its own. ChatInput is the composer alone,
> standalone React built from Carbon's `Menu`, `Theme` and icons, labs

Its nearest Carbon neighbours are `TextArea` and the input in `@carbon/ai-chat`.
Use `TextArea` for a form field; use `@carbon/ai-chat` for a whole chat
application.

sections.title: Behaviour
sections.text:
- **Two layouts.** `below` (the default) is a 48px pill with its actions in a
  row under it. `inside` puts every control in the box.
- **The box grows.** Past one row, or holding files, the pill becomes a box at
  `$border-radius-16`, with the send corner at 20 (an exploration, below). It
  grows a row at a time on Carbon's `disclosure` motion surface, to `maxRows`,
  then scrolls.
- **Send.** Always 32 (`sm`). Ghost and disabled while there is nothing to send,
  primary once there is; while `busy`, it is Stop. Enter sends and Shift+Enter
  breaks a line, or Mod+Enter sends when `submitOn` is `mod-enter`. An IME
  composition is never sent.
- **Edges, not fills.** A text-entry control never fills on hover. Its hairline
  steps from `$border-subtle` to `$border-strong` on hover, on a pointer press
  and while typing. Carbon's `$focus` ring appears only when focus arrives from
  the keyboard. A text field matches `:focus-visible` on every focus, so this is
  tracked in script.
- **Files.** `attachments` holds FileChips. Dropping or pasting files calls
  `onFilesAdded`; the composer never uploads anything itself.
- **`/` commands.** A prompt that is a single `/token` opens a listbox of the
  matching `commands`. Focus stays in the prompt (`aria-activedescendant`);
  arrows, Home and End move, Enter or Tab chooses, Escape closes and clears.
  Nothing is active when it opens, so Enter never fires a command nobody chose.

sections.title: Menus
sections.text:
`+` (add to context) and Settings open Carbon's `Menu`, upward, because the
composer sits at the foot of a view. They render **inverse**: dark on a light
page, light on a dark one, through a nested `<Theme>`, read from where the
composer sits. `menuTheme` sets it instead. Rows hover on Carbon's
`$layer-hover`. A selected row keeps Carbon's checkmark and adds the blue-gray
selected tint (a proposal, below). Model and agent mode are radio groups, with
their group names shown.

The `/` command list is drawn like these menus, in the same inverse zone.

sections.title: Explorations
sections.text:
| Exploration       | Where                           | Why                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `composer-corner` | the grown box's send corner, 20 | concentric with the 32px send control inside the 16-radius box |

sections.title: Proposals
sections.text:
| Token                           | Falls back to             | Why                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `chat-input-background`         | `$chat-prompt-background` | in dark the composer is the shell, one step below the page, so a FileChip steps up from it |
| `chat-input-menu-selected`      | `$layer-selected`         | Carbon's Menu marks selection with a checkmark only                                        |
| `chat-input-menu-selected-text` | `$text-primary`           | the brand label, solved on the tint                                                        |

V12/ChatPanels.title: ChatPanels
V12/ChatPanels.summary:
> **Problem statement:** A conversation needs its working material beside it
> (what it knows, the code it wrote, the files it was given, its settings and a
> canvas to arrange results on) without leaving the conversation to reach any of
> it.

`ChatPanels` holds which side panel is open. `ChatPanelToggles` is the row of
icon-only toggles in the surface's header, each naming its panel in a tooltip
and saying `aria-expanded`. `ChatPanelArea` is the content with the panel
opening along its inline end: pushed in a standalone chat, over the card when
embedded, and over the content below `md`.

Icon-only is a proposal: panel toggles are not on Carbon's icon-only allow-list.

V12/ChatThread.title: ChatThread
V12/ChatThread.summary:
> **Problem statement:** a chat transcript is not a list of paragraphs. A turn
> has to say who spoke without an avatar or a label, hold whatever the agent
> produced — a reasoning trace, code, a plan — and offer its controls without
> reserving a row for them on every turn. Carbon has no chat components, and the
> nearest neighbours are a plain `<ol>` and `Button`.

ChatThread is the transcript; ChatMessage is one turn in it. The user sits flush
right in a bubble at three quarters of the measure; the assistant sits flush
left at full measure, with no container, because a reply is the page's content
rather than an aside.

### What a turn does not carry

A turn has no padding and no footer at rest. The thread sets the gap —
`$spacing-08` balanced, `$spacing-07` compact — so a turn used on its own has no
orphan margin, and the actions live in that gap rather than in a row of their
own. Showing them moves nothing.

### Actions, and the time

`actions` takes `ChatMessageAction` children: a small ghost button, icon-only
with a tooltip. They appear on hover and on keyboard focus, and they stay in the
tab order while unseen, so focus can reveal them.

`timestamp` sits beside them. Leave it out when the turn carries a trace or a
plan, which already says how long the work took.

### Proposal — icon-only feedback

Thumbs up, thumbs down and regenerate are drawn icon-only. Carbon's icon-only
allow-list does not include feedback or regenerate, so this is a deliberate
proposal rather than a quiet divergence: these three are near-universal in chat,
and three labels do not fit under a turn. Each keeps a tooltip and an accessible
name.

plan, which already says how long the work took.

### Proposal — icon-only feedback

Thumbs up, thumbs down and regenerate are drawn icon-only. Carbon's icon-only
allow-list does not include feedback or regenerate, so this is a deliberate
proposal rather than a quiet divergence: these three are near-universal in chat,
and three labels do not fit under a turn. Each keeps a tooltip and an accessible
name.

V12/ChatsPanel.title: ChatsPanel
V12/ChatsPanel.summary:
> **Problem statement:** A chat surface has to let someone reach their other
> conversations without losing the one they are in, and the right way to show
> that list depends on who owns the screen. A standalone chat application can
> give the list a column of its own and push the conversation aside, because the
> layout is the chat's to spend. The same chat embedded in a product cannot: the
> product owns the layout, so the list has to borrow the space and give it
> straight back. Carbon has `SideNav` for a product's own navigation and `Menu`
> for a short list of choices, and neither answers this — a list of
> conversations is navigation inside one surface, not navigation of the
> application, and it is browsed rather than picked from. ChatsPanel is that
> list and the control that reveals it, with `presentation` deciding only
> whether it takes space or borrows it.

V12/Checkbox.title: Checkbox
V12/Checkbox.summary:
A box that turns one option on or off. A parent of partly checked children shows
mixed, a dash. `Checkbox` takes Carbon's props, plus `disabledReason` and
`timeScale`. `CheckboxGroup` sets several checkboxes under one legend, stacked
or in a row. `CheckboxSkeleton` is the checkbox while it loads.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Check:** the fill changes at once. 40ms later the check draws its stroke on,
  on fast-02 with standard-productive. The state reads first.
- **Uncheck:** the check fades out on fast-01.
- **Mixed:** the dash grows from its middle, on fast-02, 40ms after the fill. It
  is drawn from the input's own mixed state, so a click that clears it shows at
  once. Assistive tech hears "mixed".
- **Hover:** the rollover on the box. Off, a wash of the text color at 8%; on, a
  toned step of the fill. The glow fades in on fast-02 and out on fast-01. The
  box grows 1px. Hovering the label plays it too, however the label wraps.
- **Press:** no press color of its own. The box presses 1px in.
- **Status ring:** `invalid` and `warn` color the box's stroke and add 1px
  outside it, red or yellow. The rollover paints the ring, so it grows with the
  hover. Disabled and read-only show no status.
- **Message line:** helper, warning and error share one line and swap in place,
  out then in.
- **Focus:** keyboard only, 2px `$text-primary`, 2px outside the box; 3px out
  while a status shows. It has no transition.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The check and the dash appear at once. The hover changes at once. The press
still shows; the release and the return to hover are at once. The message line
changes at once.

V12/CodeSnippet.title: CodeSnippet
V12/CodeSnippet.summary:
Carbon's CodeSnippet and CodeSnippetSkeleton, prop for prop. The code sits in a
quiet well with no outline, set by `--cds-snippet-fill`. `type` is single,
inline or multi. Single and multi are a read-only textbox you can tab to, with a
copy button after it. Inline is one button round the code. A copy writes
`copyText`, or the code's text, to the clipboard, then calls `onClick`. Code
that runs past the end has a 16px soft edge there, gone while the code has
focus. A multi snippet taller than `maxCollapsedNumberOfRows` rows gets Show
more. `loading` draws the snippet as its skeleton; `CodeSnippetSkeleton` is the
same. `light` is accepted and not drawn.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Show more:** the disclosure opens the rest of the code on the travel's step,
  on entrance-productive. It shuts one step faster, on exit-productive. It is
  one layout transaction, so what sits below moves with it. The code does not
  move: the body uncovers it. The first measure lands still.
- **Soft edge, collapsed:** a 16px soft edge over the bottom of the collapsed
  code. It closes as the body lands open.
- **Label roll:** Show more rolls to Show less, whole. The chevron is the
  disclosure's motion icon, down collapsed and up expanded.
- **Copy:** single and multi use CopyButton. The Copy icon plays its action and
  the tooltip's text moves sideways to `feedback` for `feedbackTimeout`. Inline
  gives the same feedback, with the whole snippet as the trigger. The feedback
  is also read out from a polite live region.
- **Rollover:** inline, the snippet takes the rollover, its hover a step toward
  the text. Single and multi: the copy button and Show more take it.
- **Scrollbar:** the kit's Scroller pill. On multi, the down track starts below
  the copy button's 40px box.
- **Loading:** the snippet's frame, its code lines as blocks, and a disabled
  copy button. When the code arrives, the blocks dissolve in place as it fades
  up. Loading again reverses it. Inline does not load.
- **Slow motion:** `TooltipMotion`'s `timeScale` reaches the tooltip, the
  rollovers, the label roll, the scroller and Show more.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Show more opens and shuts at once, and the collapsed code has no soft edge. The
label and the tooltip's text change at once. The Copy icon's action does not
play. A rollover's press still shows; its release lands at once. The pill only
fades.

V12/CodeSnippetAlt.title: CodeSnippetAlt
V12/CodeSnippetAlt.summary:
An alternative to [CodeSnippet](?path=/docs/v12-codesnippet--overview), kept
side by side for comparison: syntax colours, inline code and a MegaButton copy
action. Its exports keep the names `CodeSnippet` and `InlineCode`.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text:
> **Problem statement:** an agent writes and runs code inside a conversation,
> and a person needs to read it there: what language it is, how long it is,
> enough of it to judge, all of it on request, and a copy that never picks up
> the line numbers. Carbon's `CodeSnippet` (multi-line) is the nearest. It has
> no syntax colour, its show-more is a flush bar, and its copy sits on the code.
> This CodeSnippet is the v12 one for conversation first: a card, a round inset
> Copy, numbered and coloured lines, and a round Show more / Show less.

sections.title: Behaviour
sections.text:
- **Collapsed** to `collapsedLines` (9) with Show more; code no longer than that
  shows whole and has no toggle. Show more opens on Carbon's disclosure motion
  (`moderate-01`, entrance easing) and becomes Show less.
- **Copy** is a round, inset ghost MegaButton. It copies `code` exactly, never
  the line numbers, which are a separate, hidden column. Its name becomes
  "Copied" for two seconds, and a status region says so.
- **Long lines scroll** sideways rather than wrapping, so numbers stay on their
  lines; the code region is in the tab order so the keyboard can scroll it.
- **Highlighting** is a small built-in lexer for the C-family and Python. Pass
  `highlight` to use a grammar (Prism, Shiki), or `false` for plain text.

sections.title: Proposals
sections.text:
Carbon ships no syntax colours. Each role is a `@carbon-proposal` token that
resolves to a Carbon tag text colour for now:
keyword and variable → `$tag-color-blue`, function → `$tag-color-green`, number
→ `$tag-color-purple`. Carbon has no orange tag, so string is proposed at orange
70 / 20 and falls back to `$tag-color-red`. Comments and punctuation are
`$text-secondary` and `$text-primary`.

V12/ContainedList.title: ContainedList
V12/ContainedList.summary:
A labelled list of items. Each `ContainedListItem` is a line of text, with an
optional icon before it and an action at its end. An item with `onClick` is a
button. `kind` sets the header: `on-page` over a hairline, or `disclosed` for a
list inside a disclosure. A `Search` as the header's `action` is the list's
search; a `Search` child sits above the items instead. The header stays at the
top while the list scrolls. `ContainedListSkeleton` is the list while it loads.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Rollover:** a clickable item takes the rollover: an even wash across the
  row, a flat press with no inset, and the release circle from the point of
  release. A motion icon plays on its hover. A static item doesn't answer the
  pointer.
- **Out:** when the items change (a search narrowing them, one removed), the
  leaving items fade where they are, on fast-01 with exit-productive. Nothing
  else moves yet. An item wanted again while it leaves fades back from where it
  is.
- **Move:** then the list's height and the items that stay move as one layout
  change, on one clock from the farthest travel. Inside another layout change,
  it joins that change's clock and lands on its frame.
- **In:** then the new items fade in where they land, on fast-02 with
  entrance-productive, staggered first to last.
- **Typing:** a change within 200ms of the one before lands at once. Whatever is
  running is cut to its end. The sequence plays for the first key after a pause.
- **Keyboard:** each clickable item is a button in the tab order. Its focus ring
  is 2px `$text-primary`, inside the item's edge.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The rollover's hover and release are at once. The items still go out, then in,
as fades on half the clock. Nothing travels: the height lands at once.

V12/ContentSwitcher.title: ContentSwitcher
V12/ContentSwitcher.summary:
Pick one of two or more options or views. The switches sit in one track, and a
selector glides between them. `ContentSwitcher` takes Carbon's API:
`selectedIndex`, `activation`, `size`, `lowContrast`, `onChange` and disabled
switches. `Switch` is a labelled switch, with an optional icon before the label.
`IconSwitch` is an icon only, named by its tooltip. `SwitchPanels` swaps the
content the selection shows.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Glide:** a new selection sends the selector from where it is to the new
  switch, on standard-productive. Its duration comes from the distance, from
  fast-00 to moderate-01. Its leading edge runs ahead, then both edges land
  together. Labels change color, and weight, where it covers them. A new
  selection mid-glide starts from where the selector is.
- **Press and reach:** the pressed switch takes a flat pressed color, inset 1px,
  while held. A press on another switch starts the selector toward it before the
  release. Slide to another switch to retarget; slide off to cancel.
- **Drag:** on by default. The selector follows the pointer and lands on the
  nearest switch, stopping at the walls with a 4px squash.
- **Hover:** unselected switches take the rollover glow and a label color step.
  The selector glows a step off its own fill under the pointer. A switch just
  picked keeps its hover until the selector lands on it. A motion icon plays on
  its switch's hover.
- **Tooltip:** on icon switches, the first tooltip snaps in from the pointer.
  While it shows, it jumps from switch to switch. The pointer can move onto it.
- **Content swap:** `SwitchPanels` swaps out, then in, never overlapping. The
  old content moves 8px the way the selector goes and fades, on fast-01 and
  exit-productive. The new content follows from 8px behind, on fast-02 and
  entrance-productive. In right to left it still follows the selector on screen.
- **Container resize:** with `fit="content"`, the default, the panels' container
  resizes to the new panel as a window, starting with the in. `fit="largest"`
  holds the largest panel's size.
- **Loading:** `loading` puts placeholder switches in the switches' own boxes,
  each label a bar. The switches take them in order as one reflow along x.
  `skeletonCount` defaults to the switches on screen, else 3.
- **Keyboard:** ← and → wrap and skip disabled switches; Home and End go to the
  ends. With `activation="automatic"` they select; with `manual` they move
  focus, and Enter or Space selects. A disabled switch with a `disabledReason`
  stays in the arrows' path and shows why in a tooltip.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
No travel: the selector fades in on the new switch as it fades out of the old,
on half the clock. There is no reach. The pressed color still shows; the hover's
release is at once. Tooltips show and leave at once, with no drift. The new
panel replaces the old on one frame, and the container resizes at once. A
loading track changes width at once.

V12/ContextualBar.title: Contextual bar
V12/ContextualBar.summary:
A bar that appears while something is true, such as a selection or unsaved
changes, and goes when it isn't. It follows `open`, and `label` names its
region. `placement="inline"`, the default, sits in the flow and opens room for
itself, so the content below glides. `overlay` floats over the content as a pill
and never takes room. `toolbar` lies over the first line of its positioned
container, in a toolbar row's place. It isn't sticky, takes no room, and hides
the row's other children while it is there. Inline and overlay bars are sticky,
8px below `--cds-contextual-bar-top`, 3rem by default. `variant="tonal"`, the
default on the page, is a fill one lightness step off its backdrop, with a
hairline. `inverse`, the default in an inset workspace, takes the page's
opposite theme. `kind` is a status. On tonal it colors the outline, solved to
3:1 against the fill. On inverse it fills the bar, stepped in lightness until
the text holds 4.5:1. A tonal bar is info unless `kind` says otherwise, and
`null` gives none. What's in it steps up one layer. Filled and outlined controls
in it step their corners down from the bar's, and ghost controls hover full
round. `ContextualBar.Count` is a number that rolls, and `ContextualBar.Swap`
swaps its content out, then in, by `swapKey`.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **One ease:** the bar's edges, its room and the mask round it move on one
  clock and one curve, standard-productive, and land on the same frame. The
  clock is the step for the farthest travel, its side edges' or its height (its
  room's, inline). Out is one step shorter. The bar doesn't fade: it travels and
  clips.
- **Snap in:** it grows from its long edge nearer the press. That edge holds
  still and the other travels away from it. It widens from 75% about the point
  across from the press, no further from the middle than `originBand` of its
  width. From a key, the key's target stands in for the press; with neither, the
  middle of its top edge. Inline and at rest, its room pushes the rows down, so
  it grows from its top edge. In a toolbar row, it grows from its bottom edge,
  at the end on the side of the press.
- **Fold out:** the far edge pulls back into the edge it grew from, with the
  width held. It shows what it last showed, not the change that closed it.
- **Content:** the row starts 8px back, against the way the bar grows, and moves
  into place over just past the bar's clock, on entrance-productive. The soft
  edge at the moving edge, `min(16px, h, H − h)`, reveals it. Out, it holds
  still while the soft edge closes over it. Reopened as it folds, it goes on
  from where it stopped.
- **Sliver guard:** the surface's opacity is `min(1, height / 4px)` in every
  placement, so it is opaque on every frame from 4px tall.
- **Content fade:** its contents wait, unseen, until the bar's start edge has
  passed them, so nothing is drawn cut. Over content, or when they wait, they
  fade up over 40ms on a clock of 220ms or less, else 80ms. Over content they
  fade out over the end of the fold.
- **Room:** inline, its room opens and closes on the bar's clock and curve in
  one layout transaction, so the content below glides. A change in its height,
  its content wrapping onto another line or back, glides too. In a container out
  of the flow it opens no room.
- **Dock mask:** carried over content, what's around it fades out like a soft
  edge: nothing shows above the bar, and the soft edge runs below it. The mask's
  strength moves on the bar's clock, and the mask follows the moving edge.
- **Count:** `ContextualBar.Count` rolls up as the number rises and down as it
  falls. Its label rolls with it.
- **Swap:** a new `swapKey` swaps the content out, then in, never overlapping.
  Its width glides from the old content's to the new, so what follows glides
  too. `axis` and `direction` set where the new content comes from.
- **Stillness:** under a still pointer, nothing it comes over or uncovers lights
  its hover until the pointer moves.
- `timeScale` slows the snap, the room, the count and the swap together.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The bar, its room and its content are there or gone at once, and the mask with
them. Inline, the scroll takes up the room, so the content below holds still on
screen. Counts change in place, and swaps snap.

V12/CopyButton.title: CopyButton
V12/CopyButton.summary:
Carbon's CopyButton, prop for prop, on the kit's IconButton. Its description is
the tooltip and the accessible name. A click turns the tooltip's text into the
feedback for `feedbackTimeout`, and another click restarts it. It does not write
the clipboard: `onClick` does. The feedback is also read out once per copy from
a polite live region. The frame is ghost by default; `frame="inset"` gives the
button its own surface. `useCopyFeedback` gives the same feedback to other
triggers.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Rollover:** IconButton's. A glow under the pointer, the 1px growth on hover
  and the press, the release circle, and a keyboard ring in the icon's color.
- **Copied mark:** a copy closes the two pages into one square, which cuts to a
  checkmark, on moderate-02. It goes back to Copy as the feedback ends, on
  moderate-01.
- **Icon hover:** the hover of whichever icon shows plays on the button's hover
  or focus.
- **Tooltip:** it arrives and leaves on the snap.
- **Feedback roll:** the description moves out to the side and the feedback
  comes in from the other, whole, on moderate-01. The tooltip resizes round the
  text as it moves. After `feedbackTimeout` it goes back the other way. If the
  pointer and focus have just left, the text waits for the tooltip to be gone,
  so a leaving tooltip never changes its text.
- **Re-placing:** the tooltip is placed again on every frame its box resizes, so
  it stays centered on the button.
- **Slow motion:** `TooltipMotion`'s `timeScale` reaches the tooltip, the
  rollover and the roll.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The icon swaps to the checkmark and back at once, and it has no hover. The text
swaps at once, with no roll. The rollover's glow, growth and release land at
once.

V12/DataTable.title: DataTable
V12/DataTable.summary:
Rows of resources in columns, with Carbon's DataTable API: its render props, its
parts and its props. `DataTable` adds `corners`: `square`, the default, or
`rounded`, 8px on the outer box. `Table` sits in the kit's Scroller, so a table
wider than its container scrolls in place. Before it scrolls, cells kept on one
line may wrap so the table fits. `TableSelectRow` and `TableSelectAll` use the
kit's Checkbox. Select-all is checked when every selectable row in view is
selected, and mixed when some are. A sortable `TableHeader` draws one motion
icon for its sort. `TableExpandRow` and `TableExpandedRow` open a row's details.
The toolbar, its search and the batch actions bar are Carbon's.
`DataTableSkeleton` is the table while it loads. `DataTableReveal` is a table
whose body loads.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Fills:** a row's hover, a selected row and a sort button change fill on the
  rollover's clocks: in on fast-02, back on fast-01, standard-productive. A
  selected row takes a 10% wash of the text color. Hover steps off the row's
  fill, over a selection or a stripe too. The toolbar search has no fill at
  rest; it takes a 5% wash on hover, on focus and once typed in, on the same
  clocks.
- **Sort icon:** a sortable header's icon is `SortDirection`, one icon for none,
  ascending and descending. A click plays its change: it shrinks to a line, then
  regrows. The unsorted icon shows only while the button is hovered or focused;
  a sorted column's always shows.
- **Expanding row:** the details push the rows below open, as one layout change.
  The height opens through a soft edge of up to 16px, on moderate-01 (160ms) for
  a 24 to 120px row, entrance-productive. The content moves 8px down into place
  over fast-02, starting once the height is half open. Shutting is one step
  faster, fast-02 (120ms), exit-productive, and the content holds still. A
  toggle mid-move turns round from where it is. The content is clipped, never
  scaled.
- **Chevron:** `ChevronDownUpToggle`, down shut and up open, on the rollover: a
  wash of the text color, 8% on hover and 16% on press.
- **Expand all:** rows that open or shut together are one motion, on one clock
  from the total travel, capped at moderate-02 (220ms) opening and 160ms
  shutting.
- **Reveal:** `DataTableReveal`'s header, column widths and selection column are
  the real table from the first frame and never move. While loading, a skeleton
  body lies over the rows' space. When the rows land, they fade in place, 30ms
  apart, as the skeleton dissolves over them. Until then the sort buttons are
  disabled and select-all is off.
- **Reflow:** in `DataTableReveal`, rows with ids reflow when they change: a
  filter, a search or a sort. Leaving rows fade where they are, on fast-01. Then
  the rows that stay and the body's height move as one layout change, on the
  farthest travel's clock. Then arriving rows fade in, staggered. Selection
  follows each row's id. A new `pageKey` is not a reflow: another page's rows
  are simply there.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Fills change at once. The sort icon changes at once. Rows open and shut at once,
with no soft edge; the content fades in on a shorter clock. A reflow keeps only
its fades, on a shorter clock.

V12/DatePicker.title: Date picker
V12/DatePicker.summary:
A date picker is a text field for a date with, in `single` and `range`, a
calendar under it. `DatePicker` holds the state and the calendar; its children
are `DatePickerInput`s, one for `simple` and `single`, two for `range`. Prop
names follow Carbon React's `DatePicker`, but this is its own implementation and
not every Carbon prop is supported: see [Component API](#component-api).

### Simple date picker

`datePickerType="simple"` renders the text field with no calendar and no
calendar icon.

### Single date picker

`datePickerType="single"` pairs the text field with a calendar. Focusing or
clicking the field opens the calendar; choosing a day fills the field.

### Range date picker

`datePickerType="range"` takes two `DatePickerInput`s. The first holds the start
date and the second the end date. Until the end is chosen, the calendar shades
the days between the start and the focused day.

### Skeleton state

`DatePickerSkeleton` is the loading placeholder. `range` draws two fields.

### AI label

`DatePickerInput` takes an AI label through `decorator`. An `AILabel` is drawn
at its `mini` size.

sections.title: Usage
sections.text:
```tsx

</DatePicker>;
```

The component uses the `Temporal` API for dates and needs `Temporal` in the
global scope. The package doesn't include a polyfill.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
None. The calendar appears and disappears at once, and its styles have no
transitions.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text: The same as above: there is no motion to reduce.

sections.title: Keyboard
sections.text:
- **Focus on a field** opens the calendar (`single` and `range`).
- **Tab** from a field opens the calendar if it is closed, and moves focus into
  it if it is open.
- **Arrow keys** move the focused day.
- **Page Up / Page Down** move a month back or forward.
- **Home / End** move to the start or end of the week.
- **Enter** selects the focused day.
- **Escape** closes the calendar.
- **Tab** from the calendar closes it and moves focus to what follows the date
  picker. **Shift+Tab** from the calendar returns focus to the field last
  focused.

When the calendar opens with no date chosen, the focused day is today.

sections.title: Accessibility
sections.text:
- Each field's label is tied to it with `for`. `required` adds an asterisk to
  the label and sets `required` on the field.
- `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`. The error, warning or helper text, whichever
  shows, is the field's `aria-describedby`.
- The calendar is `role="grid"` with the label "Calendar". Each day is a button
  named for its full date, such as "January 1, 2026". The chosen day has
  `aria-pressed`, today has `aria-current="date"`, and days outside `minDate`
  and `maxDate` are disabled buttons.
- The month buttons are named "Previous month" and "Next month".
- The calendar icon is a button named by `iconDescription` and left out of the
  Tab order.
- Month and weekday names are in English only.

sections.title: Known issues
sections.text:
- Typed text isn't kept: the field shows only a date chosen in the calendar or a
  `value` passed to `DatePickerInput`. In `simple` this means the field can't be
  filled.
- In `simple`, Tab doesn't move focus out of the field.
- `value` on `DatePicker` doesn't choose a date or fill the field. See
  [`value`](#date-picker-value).
- `DatePickerProps` declares `appendTo`, `allowInput` and `locale`, but the
  component doesn't read them. They are left out of the tables below.

sections.title: Component API
sections.text:
### `DatePicker`

| Prop             | Type                              | Default    | Description                                                                  |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`       | `ReactNode`                       | -          | The `DatePickerInput`s                                                       |
| `className`      | `string`                          | -          | Class names for the wrapper                                                  |
| `closeOnSelect`  | `boolean`                         | `true`     | Close the calendar when a date (or a range's end date) is chosen             |
| `dateFormat`     | `string`                          | `'m/d/Y'`  | How a chosen date is written in the field                                    |
| `datePickerType` | `'simple' \| 'single' \| 'range'` | `'single'` | The kind of picker                                                           |
| `light`          | `boolean`                         | `false`    | Adds the `cds--date-picker--light` class                                     |
| `maxDate`        | `string`                          | -          | The last day that can be chosen                                              |
| `minDate`        | `string`                          | -          | The first day that can be chosen                                             |
| `onChange`       | `(dates: Date[]) => void`         | -          | Called when the chosen dates change: one date, or a range's start, then both |
| `onClose`        | `() => void`                      | -          | Called when the calendar closes                                              |
| `onOpen`         | `() => void`                      | -          | Called when the calendar opens                                               |
| `readOnly`       | `boolean`                         | `false`    | Makes every field read-only                                                  |
| `short`          | `boolean`                         | `false`    | Adds the `cds--date-picker--short` class                                     |
| `value`          | `string`                          | -          | Stored on the state machine; see [`value`](#date-picker-value)               |

### `DatePickerInput`

Props not listed here are passed to the `<input>`.

| Prop              | Type                   | Default           | Description                                                        |
| ----------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `autoComplete`    | `string`               | `'off'`           | The field's `autocomplete`                                         |
| `className`       | `string`               | -                 | Class names for the field's wrapper                                |
| `decorator`       | `ReactNode`            | -                 | A decorator such as an AI label                                    |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`              | `false`           | Disables the field and its calendar icon                           |
| `helperText`      | `ReactNode`            | -                 | Text under the field, when there is no error or warning            |
| `hideIcon`        | `boolean`              | `false`           | Hides the calendar icon (always hidden in `simple`)                |
| `hideLabel`       | `boolean`              | `false`           | Hides the label visually; screen readers still read it             |
| `iconDescription` | `string`               | `'Open calendar'` | The calendar icon's accessible name                                |
| `id`              | `string`               | -                 | **Required.** The field's id                                       |
| `invalid`         | `boolean`              | `false`           | Shows the error state                                              |
| `invalidText`     | `ReactNode`            | -                 | The error message                                                  |
| `labelText`       | `ReactNode`            | -                 | The label                                                          |
| `name`            | `string`               | -                 | The field's `name`                                                 |
| `onBlur`          | `(event) => void`      | -                 | Blur handler                                                       |
| `onChange`        | `(event) => void`      | -                 | Change handler                                                     |
| `onClick`         | `(event) => void`      | -                 | Click handler                                                      |
| `onFocus`         | `(event) => void`      | -                 | Focus handler                                                      |
| `onIconClick`     | `() => void`           | -                 | Called when the calendar icon is clicked                           |
| `onKeyDown`       | `(event) => void`      | -                 | Key-down handler                                                   |
| `pattern`         | `string`               | -                 | The field's `pattern`                                              |
| `placeholder`     | `string`               | `'mm/dd/yyyy'`    | Placeholder text                                                   |
| `readOnly`        | `boolean`              | `false`           | Makes the field read-only and disables the calendar icon           |
| `required`        | `boolean`              | `false`           | Marks the field as required                                        |
| `size`            | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'`            | The field's size                                                   |
| `slug`            | `ReactNode`            | -                 | Deprecated: use `decorator`                                        |
| `type`            | `string`               | `'text'`          | The field's `type`                                                 |
| `value`           | `string`               | -                 | The field's text; when set, it is shown instead of the chosen date |
| `warn`            | `boolean`              | `false`           | Shows the warning state (ignored while `invalid`)                  |
| `warnText`        | `ReactNode`            | -                 | The warning message                                                |

Inside `DatePicker` the field is always controlled, so `defaultValue` has no
effect there.

### Date picker `dateFormat`

`dateFormat` sets how a chosen date is written in the field. The default is
`m/d/Y`. The tokens are:

- `Y`: four-digit year
- `y`: two-digit year
- `m`: month, two digits (`01`-`12`)
- `n`: month, no leading zero (`1`-`12`)
- `d`: day, two digits (`01`-`31`)
- `j`: day, no leading zero (`1`-`31`)

```tsx
</DatePicker>
```

### Date picker `minDate` and `maxDate`

Days before `minDate` or after `maxDate` are disabled in the calendar. Both
limits are inclusive. Each takes `mm/dd/yyyy` (or `m/d/yyyy`) or `yyyy-mm-dd`,
whatever `dateFormat` is.

```tsx
</DatePicker>
```

### Date picker `value`

`value` on `DatePicker` is stored on the state machine but doesn't choose a date
or fill the field. `value` on `DatePickerInput` sets the field's text, and that
text is shown while it is set.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.text:
`DatePicker` runs on the date picker state machine in
`@carbon-labs/primitives/date-picker`, which the web component date picker also
uses. The machine holds the mode, the chosen dates, the month in view and the
focused day, and maps keys to its events. The styles come from the same package.
