V12/DatePickerV2.title: Date picker and time picker
V12/DatePickerV2.summary: A date field that opens the kit's own calendar, simple, single or range, and a time field with native selects. Parts: `DatePicker`, `DatePickerInput`, `Calendar`, `DatePickerSkeleton`, `TimePicker`, `TimePickerSelect`.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
| Pattern | Where | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snap, floating profile | The calendar's surface | `snapProfileFor('popover')`: from the press on the field, or its centre from the keyboard; folds back into it on close. |
| Selection, hero | The picked day | Each month page is a selection root. A first pick grows in, 4px smaller to full over fast-02; later single picks glide by travel, 40–160ms. |
| Range ends | A range | Nothing glides: each end arrives where it is picked; the other end is painted still in the marker's colours. |
| Band | Between a range's ends | A tint of the blue into the gaps, rounded at a week's ends. The preview follows at half strength; picking the end firms it on fast-02. |
| Rollover | Days, month arrows | Press shrink, no hover expand. In-range days: a blue-contrast tint, hover only. Today: a 1px stroke that grows and presses with the hover. |
| Today picked | The selector on today | A 2px `$border-inverse` ring just outside it, 6px corner; in on fast-02, out on fast-01. |
| Tooltip | A marked day | The kit's Tooltip: the first snaps in, the next blink. Hidden during a range drag. |
| Content swap | A month change | Old days leave 8px and fade, fast-01; new ones come from 8px on the side of travel, fast-02. |
| Roll | The month's name | `RollText`, horizontal, as the days move; the year stays. |
| Reduced motion | All | The snap there or gone; the swap a snap; ends fade in place; band and ring on the half clock; tooltips blink. |

`timeScale` reaches the snap, the marker, the swap and RollText.

V12/DescriptionList.title: DescriptionList
V12/DescriptionList.summary:
Terms and their values for a details page. The list is one column, two, or by
width: two once the list itself is 672px wide, the medium size class. Each
`DescriptionListItem` is a term and its value, above it or beside it. A value is
text or any node. `copyable` adds the kit's CopyButton after the value, and
`span` runs a pair across every column. While `loading`, the terms are drawn and
each value is a bar of its line.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Skeleton hand-off:** when the values load, each bar stays over its value and
  dissolves in place on fast-01, while the value fades in on fast-02. Every fade
  is linear. Nothing slides. Loading again plays it back: the bar fades up over
  the value, which dissolves into it. Either one, interrupted, turns round from
  where it is.
- **Copy reveal:** the copy button fades in on fast-01, linear, while the pair
  is hovered or the button has focus. On touch it always shows. A click plays
  the CopyButton's own motion.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The hand-off's fades run on the reduced clock, half as long. The copy button
follows its own reduced rules.

V12/Disclosure.title: Disclosure
V12/Disclosure.summary:
A body that opens and shuts under what discloses it. It is a pair of hooks, not
a component: `useDisclosureMoves` on a root and `useDisclosureBody` on each
body. The accordion's items, the data table's expandable rows, the expandable
tile and the side nav's groups move this way. A body has three parts, each
inside the last: `.cds-disclosure__body`, a one-row grid whose height moves;
`.cds-disclosure__clip`, which clips under a soft bottom edge while it moves;
and `.cds-disclosure__content`, what is disclosed, with its padding inside the
clip.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Open:** the body's height travels on the step for its travel: under 24px
  fast-02, under 120px moderate-01, under 480px moderate-02, under 900px
  moderate-03, else slow-01. The curve is entrance-productive.
- **Shut:** one step faster, on exit-productive. The content holds still while
  the edge closes over it, and goes back above only once the body has closed.
- **Content:** it waits 8px above and comes down into place from the opening's
  first frame, over one duration token longer than the opening, on
  entrance-productive. The body lands first.
- **One motion:** every body under one root that changes in one commit moves on
  one clock: the step of the farthest travel, what is below a body included.
  With more than one body, the step is never slower than moderate-02 (220ms),
  before a shut's step down.
- **Swap:** one body opening as another shuts runs on standard-productive, with
  no step down.
- **Soft edge:** while it moves, the clip's bottom fades over
  `min(16px, h, H − h)`, so it is gone on the frame the body lands.
- **Turn:** a change mid-move starts from the body's live height and takes the
  step of what is left.
- **Still:** inside `data-still`, or with `still`, a body is open or shut at
  once.
- **List place:** `openPlace` opens a row's place in a list on its travel's
  step, entrance-productive, and brings its content down 8px into it.
  `shutPlace` closes it one step faster, on exit-productive, the content holding
  still.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
No travel: a body opens or shuts at once, with no soft edge. Its content fades
in on the reduced clock (fast-02 at half) and is gone at once. A list place is
there at once, its content fading in on the reduced clock; a leaving place goes
at once.

sections.title: Hooks
sections.text:
- `useDisclosureMoves(root, options)`: the moves of the bodies under a root.
  `options` takes `reason`, `onEnd`, `onTimed` and `timeScale`.
- `useDisclosureBody(ref, open, moves, reduced, still)`: one body's state:
  `landed`, `present`, and the `bodyProps` to spread on the body.
- `disclosureTiming(travels)` and `disclosureArrival(el, clock)`: the clock of a
  motion and the content's arrival under it, for a component that moves its own
  content.

V12/Dropdown.title: Dropdown
V12/Dropdown.summary:
A field that opens a floating list. `Dropdown` chooses one option, and
`ComboBox` is a Dropdown you can type into, its list filtered as you type.
`MultiSelect` chooses many, with a check column and a count tag in the field,
and `FilterableMultiSelect` puts its list under the ComboBox's field. They take
Carbon's props. The field is the text input's, with its label, status mark and
one message line. The list is the Menu's surface, at the field's width, five and
a half rows tall; it flips to stay on screen. `type="inline"` puts the label
beside a quiet field. The skeletons are the forms while their values load.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Snap:** the list snaps open from the press point, or from the field's center
  when a key opens it, clamped to the list's near edge.
- **Fold:** the list closes by folding its far edge back into where it came
  from. It keeps what it shows while it leaves.
- **Highlight:** the kit's highlight marker. Hover jumps it, keys glide it, and
  a held key jumps it. The first arrival grows in; every later one is simply
  there. It stays on the active option when the pointer leaves.
- **Press:** a held option's marker insets 1px.
- **Chevron:** the chevron turns while the list shows. On the Dropdown and the
  MultiSelect, the field's hover plays it; on the combo boxes, its own button's
  hover does.
- **Filter:** in the combo boxes, a key after a pause changes the list out then
  in. The options leaving fade where they are. Then the list's height and the
  options that stay move as one. Then the new options fade in. The marker comes
  back still on the active option.
- **Typing burst:** keys less than 200ms apart land at once. The rows and the
  height are simply there, and the marker stays still.
- **Reorder:** with `selectionFeedback="top"`, a choice goes out, the list makes
  room at the top, and it comes back in there. A key's choice moves at once; a
  pointer's waits until the pointer leaves the row.
- **Count tag:** the multi-selects' count snaps in with the first choice and out
  with the last. Its number rolls up as items are added and down as they go.
- **Check:** a multi-select's check column is the kit's Checkbox, which draws
  its check.
- **Soft edge:** the list scrolls on the kit's Scroller.
- **Outline ladder, error border, message line and status mark:** the text
  input's. A choice is one act, so a status shows at once.
- **Late status:** the ComboBox's errors wait for a pause in typing or for blur,
  as the text input's. `lateErrors={false}` shows them at once.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The list is there at once and gone at once. A filter or a reorder only fades,
still out then in, on half the clock. The highlight does not travel: it fades in
on the new option as it fades out of the old, on half the clock. The count tag
and the check change at once. The outline and the error border change on half of
fast-01; the message line and the status mark change at once. A rising status in
the ComboBox still waits for the pause or blur.

V12/DurationBar.title: DurationBar
V12/DurationBar.summary:
A duration on a shared scale, drawn by the Slider: the `track` shape at `sm`,
its fill the duration, with dots every 100ms, so a column of bars reads as one
scale. With `onChange` it is editable: drag the knob, press the track, use the
keys (5ms; Shift, 50ms) or type in the number field. Values snap to 5ms and stay
within 0 and `max` (default 1000). Without `onChange` it is a fixed value: a bar
to the value, no knob and no hover, a meter to assistive tech. `reference` marks
a second value, such as the last saved one. `hideNumber` hides the number. There
is no disabled state: a duration that can't be edited reads only.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
The motion is the Slider's, on the track. A fixed bar has none.

- **Glide:** a key or a click sends the knob from where it is to the new value,
  on standard-productive. Its duration comes from the distance. A held key's
  repeats move at once.
- **Press:** a press on the track starts the knob toward the pressed point. The
  release lands there.
- **Drag:** the knob follows the pointer exactly and squashes against the ends.
- **Hover and press:** hover grows the knob 2px. A pointer press takes back 1px.
  A press with no hover, a key or a touch, insets it 1px. On fast-01.
- **Fill:** rides the knob's live center on every frame. On hover it steps
  toward the knob's color and grows thicker, on fast-02, standard-productive.
- **Dots:** the dot under the pointer grows, and a press within 12px of a dot
  glides the knob there.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
No glide: the knob moves to the new value and fades in there, on half the clock.
There is no press reach. The knob's hover and press keep their clock.

V12/EasingGraph.title: EasingGraph
V12/EasingGraph.summary:
A cubic-bezier as a graph: progress up, time across, on a quarter grid with the
linear diagonal for reference. The curve is 3px solid, a `reference` curve 3px
dotted behind it, the handles' arms 2px dashed. Without `onChange` it is read
only, with the four numbers as text. With `onChange`, the two handles drag or
take the arrow keys, and the four numbers edit as one field in four segments.
Handles stay inside the unit box, so a curve never overshoots. A typed number
outside 0 to 1 is flagged and not applied.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Handle ring:** each handle is a 2px ring on the plot's fill, on the house
  rollover. The ring steps up in contrast: into hover on fast-02, to the press
  color at once, back on fast-01.
- **Handle press:** pressed or dragged, the handle grows from 12px to 18px on
  fast-01, and shrinks back on fast-02. The pointer is captured, so the press
  holds while the handle follows it.
- **Arm:** the grabbed handle's arm turns solid, in the press color, its color
  on fast-02.
- **Curve:** follows the handles and the numbers as they change, with no tween.
- **Keys:** the arrows move a handle 0.01, or 0.1 with Shift: left and right its
  x, up and down its y.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The ring and the handle's size change at once. The arm's color keeps its clock.
The curve is the same as with full motion.

V12/EmptyState.title: EmptyState
V12/EmptyState.summary:
What a region shows when it has nothing to show: first use, no results, an
error, no access. It has a visual, a required `title`, a `subtitle`, an `action`
and a `link`, and no words of its own. The visual is your own image, a still
32px `icon`, or the drawing for a `kind`; `EmptyStateArt` is that drawing alone.
`context` is the region it sits in, a page, a table's place, a panel or a tile,
and sets the size and the alignment. With no context, it is a panel on a framed
surface and a page elsewhere. It has no surface of its own.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **No motion of its own:** it is simply there. The drawings and the icon are
  still.
- **Content swap:** a swap to or from the empty state is its region's content
  swap, out then in. The old content leaves fully before the new content comes
  in, so no frame shows both. In the `ListCleared` story, the region plays it.
- **Rollover:** the action and the link take the kit Button's and Link's
  rollover. `timeScale` multiplies their clock.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The empty state has nothing of its own to change. The region's content swap is a
snap: the new content is there on the frame the old one goes. The action and the
link follow their own reduced rules.

V12/Feedback.title: Feedback
V12/Feedback.summary:
The kit's shared feedback parts, which other v12 components build on:

- `Spinner`: the loader, in six sizes, neutral or hero.
- `StatusMark`: a status's icon, with the hand-off from pending to a result.
- `CountPill`: a count whose changing digits roll.
- `SkeletonText`, `SkeletonPlaceholder` and `SkeletonOf`: loading states,
  pulsing on the skeleton wave; `SkeletonOf` draws a component as its own
  skeleton.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Nothing turns: three still dots stand in for the spinner. A status is there at
once, its glyph drawn, with no hand-off. A count's new figure fades in place on
the reduced clock, with no roll. Skeletons do not pulse; their blocks rest at
their peak.

V12/FileChip.title: FileChip
V12/FileChip.summary:
> **Problem statement:** a chat input needs to show each file a person has
> attached before they send it: what it is, whether it has uploaded, why it
> failed if it did, and a way to take it back out. Carbon has no part for this.
> `FileUploaderItem` belongs to `FileUploader`'s list, reads as a form row and
> truncates the extension away. A dismissible `Tag` is a label, with no upload
> state and no thumbnail. FileChip is one attached file, standalone, built on
> Carbon's `Loading`, `Tooltip` and icons, with a labs `MegaButton` to remove
> it. It is the first part of the chat input bar, one step lighter than the
> input: `$layer-01` on a white input, `$layer-02` on the dark shell.

Its nearest Carbon neighbours are `FileUploaderItem` and the dismissible `Tag`.
Use `FileUploaderItem` inside a `FileUploader` form; use a `Tag` for a label
that is not a file.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text:
> **Problem statement:** a chat input needs to show each file a person has
> attached before they send it: what it is, whether it has uploaded, why it
> failed if it did, and a way to take it back out. Carbon has no part for this.
> `FileUploaderItem` belongs to `FileUploader`'s list, reads as a form row and
> truncates the extension away. A dismissible `Tag` is a label, with no upload
> state and no thumbnail. FileChip is one attached file, standalone, built on
> Carbon's `Loading`, `Tooltip` and icons, with a labs `MegaButton` to remove
> it. It is the first part of the chat input bar, one step lighter than the
> input: `$layer-01` on a white input, `$layer-02` on the dark shell.

Its nearest Carbon neighbours are `FileUploaderItem` and the dismissible `Tag`.
Use `FileUploaderItem` inside a `FileUploader` form; use a `Tag` for a label
that is not a file.

sections.title: Behaviour
sections.text:
- **Kinds.** `file` shows Carbon's glyph for its extension (`Pdf`, `Doc`, `Txt`,
  `Csv`, `Zip`, `Xls`, `Ppt`, `Json`, else `Document`). `image` and `video` show
  a thumbnail, without the name unless `showName` is set. A video's thumbnail
  carries Carbon's `VideoFilled` at 12 on a 16px round `$overlay` backing: a
  type marker, not a play button, since the chip body does nothing. The 12px
  size is a proposal (see below); on stock Carbon it is 16. The kind follows
  `mimeType` unless `kind` is given.
- **Status.** `uploading` shows Carbon's small `Loading`. `error` shows
  `ErrorFilled`, and the second line says why, so a failure is never told by
  colour alone; a media chip in error also shows its name. `complete` shows
  `CheckmarkFilled`, holds for `successDelay` (1500ms, InlineLoading's default),
  fades, and calls `onSuccessEnd`.
- **Names truncate in the middle.** The end, the last four characters and the
  extension, never shrinks. The full name is always the chip's accessible name,
  and it is in the Remove button's label and tooltip. When the name is actually
  cut, resting the pointer on it for `nameTooltipDelay` (1000ms) shows the full
  name in a Carbon `Tooltip`; a name that fits gets none.
- **Not text.** The pointer stays the default arrow over the chip; only Remove
  shows Carbon's button cursor.
- **Remove is the only control,** a `MegaButton` (ghost, `xs`, icon-only,
  `Close`) named "Remove `name`". The chip plays its exit, then calls
  `onRemove`. Under reduced motion it calls at once. Moving focus afterwards is
  the input bar's job.
- **Motion.** Enter: opacity and a slight scale over `$duration-moderate-02`,
  entrance productive. Exit and the check's fade: opacity over
  `$duration-fast-02`, exit productive. Reduced motion: none.

sections.title: Explorations
sections.text:
- **`radius-field` (6dp).** FileChip's corner, and its thumbnail at the radius
  less the 2dp inset. It is tried on this component only; Carbon's tags are 4dp,
  and on stock Carbon the reference is the only thing to change.

sections.title: Proposals
sections.text:
- **`file-chip-background`.** The chip's fill: `{layer-01}` in light and
  `{layer-02}` in dark, one step lighter than the chat input (white in light,
  the shell, `$layer-03`, in dark). No Carbon token is both; on stock Carbon it
  is `$layer-01`, which in v12 dark is the input's own value.
- **`file-chip-video-icon-size` (12px, `$spacing-04`).** The video glyph on its
  16px backing. Carbon's icons start at 16, which fills the backing and reads
  too large on a 36px thumbnail. Read through `get-var` with Carbon's 16 as the
  fallback; the stories' `proposals` control turns it off to compare.

sections.title: Getting started

V12/FileUploader.title: FileUploader
V12/FileUploader.summary:
Carbon's file uploader, with its props. `FileUploader` is a title, a
description, an add button and the files it has added, all with one
`filenameStatus`; its ref clears them (`clearFiles()`). For an uploader the app
builds itself, the parts are `FileUploaderButton`, `FileUploaderDropContainer`,
`FileUploaderItem` and `FileUploaderSkeleton`. Each file is an item on the quiet
surface with one status slot: a progress mark while it uploads and once it is
complete, and a remove button to edit. With `progress`, a known size, the mark
is a ring that fills by it; without, it is the Spinner. `arrive={false}` lists a
file with no motion, as for files already there on load.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Arrive:** an item opens its place in the list as it mounts, as a disclosure:
  on its travel's step, the content following from half the open. What is below
  moves with it.
- **Arrival stagger:** items added in one commit open in document order on a
  stagger. Its step comes from the items' pitch, and the last starts within the
  stagger window.
- **Status hand-off:** uploading and complete are one mark, the ProgressRing at
  16px. Complete is that mark changing in place: the ring completes, then it
  shrinks 4px, the success disc grows from 4px under its size, and the check
  draws on.
- **Face swap:** a change between the progress mark and the remove button is a
  content swap in place. The old face fades fully out, then the new fades in,
  with no travel.
- **Error:** an invalid item's error opens under the name as its own disclosure
  body, so the item grows. The new face waits for that move to land. The warning
  mark plays its motion icon once it has landed.
- **Leave:** a removed item leaves a copy where it stood, and the copy's place
  closes, one step faster, its content held still. Items removed together each
  rise 8px and fade out in order, then close as one motion.
- **Drag-over:** with a file held over the drop zone, the rollover's hover glow
  follows the file and a 2px blue ring fades in inside the edge, in on
  `fast-02`, out on `fast-01`. Moving onto a child of the zone does not end it.
- **Rollover:** the drop zone, the remove button and the add button take the
  kit's rollover.
- **Label roll:** the add button's label changes to the chosen file's name, or
  "N files", through RollText, so only the parts that change roll.
  `disableLabelChanges` keeps the label.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
No travel and no stagger: an item is there, or gone, at once, and so is its
error. The faces snap and the marks do not beat. The ring and the glow on the
drop zone are there or gone at once. The add button's label swaps in place.

V12/FilterPanel.title: Filter panel
V12/FilterPanel.summary:
Narrow a long list. Filters opens a side panel with one section per field
(status, region, environment and so on). Each option shows how many items it
would match. Apply filters the list; the filters in use show as tags above it,
where each can be removed. `FilterPanel` is the panel, on the kit's SidePanel;
`FilterSummary` is the row of tags.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
| Pattern                   | Where                                                   | Values                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Disclosure                | A section opening or shutting                           | The accordion's: duration by travel, the content 8px back moving from the first frame; shutting a step faster              |
| The panel's snap and push | Opening and closing                                     | SidePanel's own frames: inset by its edge; pushed beside the page where the shell has room, over it otherwise              |
| Content movement in place | Each option's count, the results line                   | RollText: only the figures that change roll, on moderate-01; the label holds still                                         |
| List presence             | A section's search narrowing its options                | Out on fast-02, one move by travel, in on moderate-01, staggered                                                           |
| The tags' snap from below | A filter applied appears in the summary                 | The Tag's snap in: from a few px under its height, moderate-01, entrance-productive, once the tags after it have made room |
| Removal                   | A tag dismissed, or a filter cleared in the panel       | It snaps out on the Tag's fast-02 while the rest close the gap by travel                                                   |
| Room                      | The summary's row coming or going in the resource index | The recipe's filters room: opens on its travel, shuts a step faster                                                        |
| Reduced motion            | Everywhere                                              | Sections open and shut at once; counts and tags change at once; the panel's reduced fade                                   |

V12/FormLayout.title: Form layout
V12/FormLayout.summary:
One layout for settings, create and edit forms. `FormLayout` is the form and its
widest: narrow 320px, medium 640px by default, wide 960px or full. `as="div"`
puts it inside another form. `FormSection` is a title, a description 8px under
it and its fields 24px below, in a fieldset. `FormRow` puts fields side by side
from a 480px form, 16px apart, and stacks them under it; `columns` sets how
many. Sections are 48px apart and fields 32px, the room a field's message line
opens into. A layout's or a section's `disabled` and `readOnly` reach every
field in it: the kit's fields read them with `useFormFieldState`, and a disabled
section also disables any other control in it. `UnsavedChangesBar` holds Save
and Discard at the bottom of its scroll while the form has changes, with
`useDirtyForm` to track them. `SavingStatus` shows where a save stands.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **None:** a form holds still while it is filled in. Rows restack at once when
  the form crosses 480px. Each field keeps its own motion.
- **Save:** the unsaved changes bar arrives on the first change and holds still
  after. It snaps in from its bottom edge, opaque from 4px. Its content moves
  8px up into place from the first frame and lands just after the bar. The clock
  is the step for the bar's height, on entrance-productive. Leaving, its top
  edge folds back down a step faster, on exit-productive, and the content holds
  still.
- **Save swap:** the bar's message and actions swap in place, for the discard
  question and a failed save. The count rolls to each new number.
- **Saving status:** the mark hands off from one status to the next. The spinner
  shrinks 4px, the disc grows in, and the check or slash draws on, with no
  fades. The label swaps in place, out then in, on the content swap's clocks.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The layout has nothing to change. The bar only fades, at its final geometry, on
the reduced clock. Its swaps change at once. The saving status's mark and label
change at once.

V12/FullPageError.title: FullPageError
V12/FullPageError.summary:
A whole page that says something went wrong: a 403, a 404, or a custom error.
Its props are the Carbon Products FullPageError's.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- The label's arrow draws: its line from the top, down and right, and its head
  grows from the tip before the line ends.
- The error (label and title) fades in as the head draws; then the description,
  actions and art fade in.
- A new error on a mounted page swaps out, then in.
- Held still while it is off screen.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text: No drawing: the page fades in at once, on the reduced clock.

V12/HistoryRail.title: HistoryRail
V12/HistoryRail.summary:
> **Problem statement:** an agent's work goes through many iterations, and a
> person needs to find one of them — the version before the table was replaced,
> the run that failed — without reading the whole conversation again. A list of
> links costs a line each and buries the shape of the history. Carbon has no
> scrubber; the nearest neighbours are `Slider` and a list.

HistoryRail is a scrubber: a column of marks down the edge of the panel, one per
iteration, with the live one drawn as a square. Moving a pointer down the track
or arrowing through it lights the nearest iteration and opens a card saying what
changed there.

### One control, not one per mark

The whole track takes the pointer and resolves to the nearest iteration. That is
what lets the marks sit 14px apart and stay hittable: there is a single 24 x 196
target rather than fourteen small ones, so WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size is met
outright, on a mouse and under a finger alike. A mark is decoration —
`aria-hidden`, no focus, no pointer region of its own — and it grows in place
when it lights, so nothing ever moves under a pointer in flight.

### What it says

The rail is a `slider`: one tab stop, `aria-valuenow` on the position and
`aria-valuetext` naming the iteration and what changed. The card repeats those
words for the eye, so it is hidden from assistive technology rather than read
out twice. Pass `translations.valueText` to change the sentence.

### Current is not the same as selected

`current` is the live iteration — the state of the work — and stays put as you
scrub. `value` is the one you are looking at. They are usually different, which
is the point: you can look back without leaving where you are.

V12/IconMotion.title: IconMotion
V12/IconMotion.summary:
Makes the motion icons follow the kit's reduced motion. Without it, a motion
icon looks only at its own `animated` prop, the nearest `MotionIconProvider`
and the OS, so a `MotionProvider level="reduced"` would leave icons moving.

- `FollowKitMotion` wraps its children in a `MotionIconProvider` set from the
  nearest `MotionProvider`'s level, else the OS. Put it inside each
  `MotionProvider` that sets a level. An icon's own `animated` still wins.
- `useIconAnimated()` returns the same boolean, for a component that passes
  `animated` to an icon it draws.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Under the OS setting, icons use the motion icons' reduced mode: the rest
shape, with changes at once. Under a reduced level while the OS does not
reduce, icons draw still.

V12/Illustrations.title: Illustrations
V12/Illustrations.summary:
Line drawings in isometric projection for empty states and tiles, drawn with
hidden lines and no fills.

V12/InlineEdit.title: InlineEdit
V12/InlineEdit.summary:
A value shown as text that turns into its field in place. The view is the text,
a slot for a status mark and an edit button. The field is a text input, a text
area or a select, with save and cancel buttons. Press the view or the edit
button to open the field. Enter saves; in a text area, Shift+Enter breaks a
line. Escape cancels. Focus goes to the field, its text selected, and back to
the edit button on save or cancel. `validate` checks the draft on save. A save
that returns a promise shows saving, and a rejection reopens the field with its
message. Read-only and disabled values show a lock or a crossed pencil, with
`reason` in its tooltip.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Content swap in place:** the text and the field swap in place, out then in,
  by fade only. The old face fades out on fast-01, then the new one fades in on
  fast-02.
- **Layout move:** when the faces differ in size, the box holds its old size,
  then moves to the new one on the step for its travel, on standard-productive.
  The new face arrives once it lands.
- **Mark snap:** save and cancel snap in as the field arrives. Each is opaque at
  half size, then grows to full on fast-02, entrance-productive.
- **Status hand-off:** a save that returns a promise closes the field at once,
  with a spinner beside the new value. When it resolves, the spinner hands off
  to a check: it shrinks, the disc grows and the check draws on. A save that
  returns nothing shows the check alone. The check holds for `savedHold` (1500ms
  by default), then fades on fast-02.
- **Validation:** an error keeps the field open and shows on the field's message
  line without waiting for a pause. While it shows, each change checks the draft
  again.
- **Quiet hover:** the view takes the rollover's even wash, flat on press. The
  edit button fades in on hover or focus, on fast-01. Where there is no hover,
  it always shows.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The faces swap at once, and the box takes its new size at once. Save and cancel
are there at once. The status mark is simply there, and the check goes at once
after its hold. `reduced` overrides the preference.

V12/JobsTray.title: JobsTray
V12/JobsTray.summary:
Background jobs in a panel from the header, with no Carbon counterpart. Each job
has a title, a ProgressBar, a StatusIndicator, and Cancel or Retry. A job is
`queued`, `running`, `finished`, `failed` or `cancelled`; its `progress` is 0 to
100, and a running job with none is indeterminate. The host owns `open` and
`jobs`. A press outside, or Escape, calls `onClickOutside`, and Escape puts
focus back on the trigger. `JobsTrayIndicator` is the trigger's face: put it in
the header's IconButton, and name the button with the count and the status
(`jobsStatus`, `jobsStatusLabel`).

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Open:** the floating snap from its trigger, timed by size. A tray over 320px
  takes the surface rule's clocks. The presence fade runs with it. Closing, the
  far edge folds back.
- **Progress:** each job's bar retargets as progress comes in, and travels only
  on an update. Done, the bar sits full; queued, empty.
- **Status:** the StatusIndicator hands off from pending to the job's end.
- **Arrive:** a job added while the tray is open opens its place.
- **Clear finished:** each ended job's place shuts. Once the list is empty, the
  empty text comes in after the places have shut.
- **Trigger mark:** the activity icon carries a status mark in its corner:
  pending while any job is at work, then failed if any ended failed, else done.
  The mark stays while ended jobs are in the tray; once cleared, the plain icon
  is back. The mark comes in, changes and goes on its own motion.
- **Count:** the jobs still working, on the CountPill, whose digits roll.
- **Toast:** a job that ends while the tray is closed shows one quiet toast,
  grouped with the others, and never again for that run. A success leaves after
  5 seconds; a failure stays. A retry starts a new run. It toasts only where a
  `ToastStack` is above it, and not with `toast={false}`.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The tray fades in place. Places open and shut at once. The trigger's mark is
there at once, with pending as still dots. The bar and the count take their own
reduced motion.

V12/JumpTo.title: JumpTo
V12/JumpTo.summary:
A floating pill back to a point in a scrolled container. It shows while its
target is out of view by more than `threshold`, and hides when the target is
back. It sits at the top or the bottom center of the view, with an arrow toward
the target. A preset sets the target, the words and where the target lands:
Latest (the live edge, counting what arrives), Unread, Top, Selection or
Current. The pill is the kit Button, tonal, and takes no room in the layout. A
count is announced in a polite live region. `useJumpTo` is the same without the
pill, for a host that draws its own control.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **4px arrival:** the pill arrives from 4px short of its measured width and
  height, about its center, on fast-02 with the entrance-snap curve, as it fades
  in. It leaves to the same size on fast-01, exit-productive. When the target
  moves to the other side, the pill leaves, then arrives at its new place.
- **Scroll glide:** a jump glides the container to the target, on a clock set by
  the distance, with the standard-productive curve. Past two views, it first
  moves to one view short of the target, then glides the rest. A reader's own
  wheel, touch, key or press stops the glide where it is.
- **Stick to end:** with Latest, a view at the end stays there as content grows.
  A reader's own scroll toward the start lets go once it settles.
- **Keyboard:** Enter or Space on the pill jumps and moves focus to the target,
  or to the container. A pointer press leaves focus where it is.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The jump lands at once, with no glide. The pill only fades, in and out.
`reduced` overrides the preference.

V12/KeyboardShortcut.title: KeyboardShortcut
V12/KeyboardShortcut.summary:
> **Problem statement:** Carbon can show a keyboard shortcut only as a plain
> string in `MenuItem`'s `shortcut` prop. Every product hand-types its own
> glyphs, shows `⌘` to Windows users or `Ctrl` to Mac users, and leaves screen
> readers to announce `⌘` as "place of interest sign". `KeyboardShortcut` takes
> the keys once (`keys={['mod', 'K']}`), shows `⌘K` on macOS and `Ctrl+K`
> elsewhere, and names the combination in words ("Command K"). Its nearest
> Carbon neighbour is `MenuItem.shortcut`, and `kind="plain"` matches it.

It only **displays** a shortcut. Like `MenuItem.shortcut`, it never registers or
listens for the keys.

`kind="plain"` is text only:

sections.title: Overview
sections.text:
> **Problem statement:** Carbon can show a keyboard shortcut only as a plain
> string in `MenuItem`'s `shortcut` prop. Every product hand-types its own
> glyphs, shows `⌘` to Windows users or `Ctrl` to Mac users, and leaves screen
> readers to announce `⌘` as "place of interest sign". `KeyboardShortcut` takes
> the keys once (`keys={['mod', 'K']}`), shows `⌘K` on macOS and `Ctrl+K`
> elsewhere, and names the combination in words ("Command K"). Its nearest
> Carbon neighbour is `MenuItem.shortcut`, and `kind="plain"` matches it.

It only **displays** a shortcut. Like `MenuItem.shortcut`, it never registers or
listens for the keys.

`kind="plain"` is text only:

sections.title: Platforms
sections.text:
`mod` is ⌘ on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, and `remove` is ⌫ on macOS and Del
elsewhere. macOS shows glyphs (⌘ ⌥ ⇧ ⌃ ↩ ⌫ ⎋ ←); Windows and Linux show words
(Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win, Enter). Modifiers are shown in each platform's order —
⌃⌥⇧⌘ on macOS, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Win elsewhere — whatever order they are written
in, and the spoken name follows the same order. `platform="auto"` detects it in
the browser. A server render cannot know the platform, so it renders the Windows
and Linux words and the browser takes over straight after hydration. Pass
`platform="mac"` or `"other"` when the server knows better, for example from the
request's `User-Agent`.

sections.title: Accessibility
sections.text:
- The markup is the HTML standard's own for a key combination: one `<kbd>` per
  key inside an outer `<kbd>`.
- The whole shortcut is named in words, through visually hidden text. A `<kbd>`
  has the generic role, which ARIA 1.2 forbids naming, so `aria-label` on it is
  dropped or read inconsistently. The glyph keys are hidden from assistive
  technology so the name is not read twice.
- Inside a control, the words become part of its name: a menu item reads "Copy
  Command C", not "Copy ⌘C".
- `translateWithId` translates both what each key shows and its spoken name,
  with separate ids: `carbon.keyboard-shortcut.control.label` ("Strg") and
  `carbon.keyboard-shortcut.control.name` ("Steuerung").
- In a right-to-left page the combination stays left to right, as on the
  keyboard.

sections.title: On surfaces
sections.text:
- **In a tooltip.** Inside Carbon's high-contrast popover (`Tooltip`,
  `DefinitionTooltip`, an `IconButton`'s label), keycaps take Carbon's inverse
  family by themselves: `$background-inverse-hover` fill, `$border-inverse`
  edge, `$text-inverse` label. `kind="plain"` inherits the popover's text
  colour. Nothing to set.

- **On a Tile or any other layer.** A keycap's fill is the contextual `$layer`,
  so directly on a `Tile` it is the tile's own colour and only its border draws
  the key. Put the content in a `<Layer>` inside the tile, as Carbon does for
  any control on a layer; or use `kind="plain"` where a keycap is not wanted.

sections.title: Inside a menu
sections.text:
Left, Carbon's `MenuItem` with its own `shortcut` strings; right,
`KeyboardShortcut kind="plain"` in the same slot.

V12/KitDefaults.title: KitDefaults
V12/KitDefaults.summary:
`KitDefaults` sets `density`, `corners`, `containerCorners`, `variant`, `brand`,
`frame` and `shadow` for everything inside it. A component uses them only for a
prop it isn't given, so **its own prop always wins**. With no provider, every
component keeps its own defaults. Recipes use it per region (a filter bar is
usually `compact`); see `../recipes/README.md` ("Density").

```tsx

</KitDefaults>
```

V12/Link.title: Link
V12/Link.summary: Carbon's Link, prop for prop, on the rollover's text standard in link blue: the text, an underline and an optional icon after it.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
| Pattern | Where | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rollover, link blue | The whole link | A glow of the dimmed colour in the letters under the pointer, fast-02 in, fast-01 out, growing 80% to 100% over moderate-02; press dimmer, flat; the release circle |
| Colours | Every state | Matched lightness in the blue's own hue; the rest is `link-primary` in every theme |
| Underline, standalone | On hover | The rollover-text underline layer, fading in over fast-02 and out over fast-01 |
| Underline, inline | Always | A real text decoration under the letters' paint, so it takes the glow and press with them |
| Motion icon | `renderIcon` | The icon's hover plays on the link's hover or keyboard focus; it dims with the text, flatly |
| Slow motion | All | The CSS steps read the duration tokens' variables; the release circle takes `timeScale` |
| Reduced motion | All | The hover still dims and the press still shows; the release and the hover's return take 1ms |

Reduced motion comes from a TooltipMotion `reduced`, else the provider,
else the system. See "reduced" in props.md.

V12/List.title: List
V12/List.summary:
Carbon's UnorderedList, OrderedList and ListItem: static text lists, their
markers one step under their text.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
| Pattern        | Where    | Values                                                        |
| -------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| None           | The list | A list is content, principle 5: it doesn't answer the pointer |
| Reduced motion | The list | Nothing changes                                               |

V12/ListReflow.title: ListReflow
V12/ListReflow.summary:
A short row whose items come and go (a breadcrumb's trail, the page numbers in a
pagination nav), moved as one change: items that leave fade where they stood,
the rest slide to their new places.

V12/Loading.title: Loading
V12/Loading.summary: `Loading` and `InlineLoading`, with Carbon's props, on the kit's one spinner.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Start:** the arc draws on, its tail lengthening back from its head; an
  overlay fades up on that clock.
- **Stop:** `active={false}`: the tail catches up with the head, and the spinner
  shrinks to half and fades in its last frames.
- **Gate:** `delay` and `minDuration` show nothing for the first `delay` ms,
  then keep the spinner at least `minDuration` ms once it shows. Both default to
  0, as in Carbon.
- **InlineLoading:** a change of status changes the mark in place: the spinner
  shrinks, the result's disc grows, then its check or slash draws on. The text
  swaps out, then in, on the same clocks.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Nothing turns: three still dots stand in for the arc, there or gone at once. The
overlay fades on the reduced clock. InlineLoading's mark changes at once and its
text snaps; the words carry the state.

V12/MegaButton.title: MegaButton
V12/MegaButton.summary:
> **Problem statement:** products reach for a button with a visible keyboard
> shortcut, and for one API across text, icon-and-text and icon-only buttons.
> Carbon's `Button` has no key command, trails its only icon, and hands
> icon-only to `IconButton`, which has no danger kinds. MegaButton is one button
> for all of it, and the place to see, side by side with Carbon's `Button`,
> three positions put to Carbon: primary rests neutral and turns blue only when
> the person acts; blue responds on every kind; and colour is authored in OKLCH,
> each value a lightness on a hue and chroma curve.

Its nearest Carbon neighbours are `Button` and `IconButton`. Use those when you
need none of the above.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text:
> **Problem statement:** products reach for a button with a visible keyboard
> shortcut, and for one API across text, icon-and-text and icon-only buttons.
> Carbon's `Button` has no key command, trails its only icon, and hands
> icon-only to `IconButton`, which has no danger kinds. MegaButton is one button
> for all of it, and the place to see, side by side with Carbon's `Button`,
> three positions put to Carbon: primary rests neutral and turns blue only when
> the person acts; blue responds on every kind; and colour is authored in OKLCH,
> each value a lightness on a hue and chroma curve.

Its nearest Carbon neighbours are `Button` and `IconButton`. Use those when you
need none of the above.

sections.title: How it differs from Carbon's Button
sections.text:
- **Kinds.** `primary` (neutral at rest), `secondary` (the outline), `tertiary`
  (a tinted fill), `ghost`, `danger` and `danger--secondary` (a red outline).
  Carbon's names for the outline and the fill are the other way round: the swap
  is deliberate, because the outline reads better beside a neutral primary.
- **Content.** Text, icon and text with the one icon leading or trailing, or
  icon-only (`xs` to `lg`), every kind including danger.
- **Key command.** `keyCommand={['mod', 's']}` shows the chord last, with
  `KeyboardShortcut`, and announces it through `aria-keyshortcuts`. The button
  is named by its label alone. Icon-only buttons put the chord in the tooltip.
- **Sizes.** Carbon's six heights, from the layout context. Inline padding grows
  with size (12, 16, 20, 24px) where Carbon's stays at 16px.
- **Press.** The background fades slowly into the pressed colour while a soft,
  edgeless radial of the same colour grows from where the pointer went down,
  timed by Carbon's motion tokens. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the colour
  changes at once.
- **Focus** is Carbon's: a 2px ring over a 1px gap, drawn inside.

sections.title: Proposals
sections.text:
Every value Carbon does not have is a `@carbon-proposal`, read with a Carbon
fallback so the component renders on stock Carbon. The **proposals** control
switches them on and off. The token values live in `proposals/tokens.json`,
shaped like Carbon's `packages/themes` DTCG, with each colour's OKLCH curve and
its sRGB fallback beside Carbon's per-theme value.
