V12/Menu.title: Menu
V12/Menu.summary:
A floating list of actions and choices, with Carbon's API: `MenuItem`,
`MenuItemSelectable`, `MenuItemRadioGroup`, `MenuItemGroup` and
`MenuItemDivider`, and a MenuItem's own MenuItems as a submenu. `MenuButton` and
`OverflowMenu` open one from a button, as SplitButton does; `x` and `y` place
one at a point, as a context menu. One highlight serves the pointer and the
keys, and labels take its color where it covers them. With `inline`, the menu is
drawn in place, with no portal, placement, snap or close.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Open:** the frame grows about its cause: the press that opened it, else the
  trigger's center, as from the keyboard. `openFrom="trigger"` on a button
  always starts at its center.
- **Content:** the list slides out of the frame on y only.
- **Fade:** it fades up over the first part of the open and out over the last
  part of the close: 40ms on a clock of 220ms or less, else 80ms.
  `exitFade={false}` folds back opaque.
- **Close:** the far edge folds back into the point it grew from, the list
  still. It is gone on the fold's last frame. Reopened while it leaves, it turns
  round from where it is.
- **Highlight:** its first arrival in an open menu grows in from the row's
  center. Under the pointer it jumps from row to row. The arrow keys glide it,
  timed by travel. It shrinks back and fades when the pointer leaves the list.
- **Danger:** on a danger row the highlight turns to the danger button's color,
  on the glide's clock.
- **Press:** the highlight insets 1px while a row is held.
- **Submenu:** one level deep, marked by a chevron. It opens beside its row
  after 100ms of hover, or on → or Enter, and snaps from the row. ← and Escape
  go back.
- **Chevron:** on MenuButton, the chevron turns while the menu shows.
- **Keyboard:** ↑ and ↓ wrap; Home, End and typeahead move too. Disabled rows
  are skipped unless they have a `disabledReason`. A radio group's `shortcuts`
  win over typeahead. A trigger opens on the first row with Enter, Space or ↓,
  and on the last with ↑.
- **Cast shadow:** off by default. `shadow` turns it on; it grows and folds with
  the frame.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The menu and its submenus are there at once and gone at once: no growth, slide,
fold or fade. The highlight does not travel: it fades in on the new row as it
fades out of the old, on half the clock. A menu placed again while open moves at
once.

V12/Modal.title: Modal
V12/Modal.summary:
A centred dialog over a dimmed page, with Carbon's props. `Modal` is one piece
and controlled: every way of closing calls `onRequestClose`, and only `open`
closes it. `ComposedModal` is its shell, built from `ModalHeader`, `ModalBody`
and `ModalFooter`; it closes itself unless `onClose` returns `false`. A passive
modal has no footer. The body scrolls when it overflows, and the footer's
primary button can show a loading status.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Overlay:** the dim fades in over moderate-01 (entrance-productive) and out
  over fast-02 (exit-productive), from wherever it is.
- **Snap arrival:** the frame grows to its place in the centre, from 92% of its
  box on each axis, or 16px in on a side where that is more. It runs over
  fast-02 on entrance-snap. The content moves in with it on y.
- **Cursor origin:** it grows from its top or bottom edge facing the press that
  opened it, at the press's x. Opened from a key, it grows from the focused
  launcher's centre the same way. With no launcher, it grows from its own
  centre.
- **Pull-back:** leaving, the frame shrinks back to the same start, toward the
  same origin, over fast-01 on exit-pullback, fading as it goes. Reopened while
  it leaves, it turns round from where it is.
- **Page recede and blur:** the page behind draws back to 99% about the
  viewport's centre, under one even blur, on the overlay's clocks. `backdrop`
  leaves either out.
- **Content swap:** a new `swapKey` on `ModalBody` swaps its content. The old
  content leaves 16px up over fast-01, fading, then the new content enters from
  16px below over fast-02. The height holds through the out, then glides with
  the in, and the modal re-centres. The primary button's loading label swaps the
  same way, its width gliding.
- **Loading:** the mark at the primary button's end changes in place, from the
  spinner to the check or the error mark. `onLoadingSuccess` is called 1.5s
  after `finished`.
- **Cast shadow:** off by default; `shadow` turns it on. It grows and pulls back
  with the frame. While the pointer is over or near the modal, the shadow falls
  away from it, and it eases back to rest when the pointer leaves.
- **Focus:** focus moves in on open and Tab wraps inside. Focus goes back to
  `launcherButtonRef`, else to what had it, as the modal starts to leave.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The overlay and the surface only fade, at their final geometry, on half the
clock. The blur is there at once, and the page doesn't scale. A content swap
shows the new content at once, with no fade or glide. The shadow's light moves
at once.

V12/MotionIcons.title: Motion icons
V12/MotionIcons.summary: Carbon's UI icons that move: each matches its Carbon icon at rest, size for size. It moves on hover; a toggle switches between two Carbon drawings; some icons take a status mark or play an action.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
| Pattern | Where | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hover | The icon, or the nearest `data-motion-icon-frame` ancestor; keyboard focus on that frame | 160ms entrance in, 120ms exit out; constant 2px line weight; touch never plays it |
| Toggle | A `…Toggle` icon on a change of state | One drawing becomes the other: a slash, a fill or a match cut, per icon |
| Status mark | A status icon's corner | Draws in over moderate-01, leaves over fast-02; a knockout keeps the mark clear of the drawing |
| Pending | A status icon's corner | The loading arc, one turn a second, on the page's shared loading phase |
| Action | `actionKey`, `actionOn="click"` or the ref's `trigger()` | One-shot inside the 36×36 box, or a loop; may hand off to a status; the hover waits for it |
| Press | An icon that is the control | 1px in on every side while held; release over fast-02, exit easing |
| Reduced motion | All | Still by default; pending shows three still dots; no press |

V12/Notification.title: Notification
V12/Notification.summary:
Inline, toast and actionable notifications, and the callout, with Carbon's
props: the six kinds, `title`, `subtitle`, `caption`, `lowContrast`,
`hideCloseButton`, `role`, a toast's `timeout` and `onClose`. A plain surface
whose outline, in the status color, says the kind. `variant` picks outlined,
inverse or tonal; by default errors and actionable notifications are inverse,
the rest outlined. `ToastStack` is the one place toasts live, and `useToasts`
shows and closes them from anywhere inside it. `StaticNotification` is the
callout's deprecated name.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Arrive:** the snap from the top center. The container grows, the content
  slides on y, and nothing else moves. `from` grows it from a control instead.
  With `arrive={false}` it is part of the page from the start, as a callout is.
- **Leave:** the far edge folds back into the top center it grew from.
- **Inline place:** an inline notification opens its place in the page as it
  arrives and closes it as it leaves, on one clock. What is below it follows.
- **Status mark:** the mark plays its motion icon once it has landed. With
  `icon`, an action icon loads in with its status; with `pending`, it shows its
  spinner until the kind changes. A change of kind is a match cut.
- **Update in place:** new words, from an update by id or a group's next member,
  swap out, then in. No frame shows both. The status turns on the empty card
  between them, and so does a change of height, timed by its travel.
- **Timer:** a toast's timeout you can see, as a ring round the close button or
  a bar under the text (`timer`). Hover or focus pauses it.
- **Buttons:** the close and action buttons take the rollover. The close
  button's icon is a motion icon.
- **Focus:** closed with focus inside, focus moves to the next toast, or back
  where it came from.

### Toast stack

- **Deck:** the newest toast in front, the next two behind it, each 8px below
  the one in front and inset 6px a side. Their content is faded out, and each
  further back is dimmer.
- **Front change:** with `frontChange="swap"` (the default) the front stays one
  surface. A new toast turns it to its own outline, fill and height while the
  text crossfades in place, and the old front steps down the stack behind it.
  The snap plays only into an empty deck and out of a last card. With `snap`,
  every arrival and exit snaps.
- **One move:** every change in the deck starts on the same frame and runs on
  one clock and one curve.
- **Open:** hover or focus deals the deck into a list, newest at the top.
  Leaving closes it after a beat. On touch, a tap opens it and a tap elsewhere
  closes it.
- **Cap:** `cap` toasts at once (3). One more pushes the oldest to the back,
  where it fades out. An error, or a toast asking for action, is never pushed
  out.
- **Missed:** a toast that times out or is pushed out is counted (`onMissed`) on
  the frame it starts to go. A toast the person closes just leaves.
- **Group:** `show` with a `group` already showing merges into that toast. Its
  count rolls up, its text and kind become the latest, and it comes to the
  front.
- **Burst:** of toasts shown at once, only the newest arrives. The ones behind
  it fade in at their places once it has landed.
- **Swipe:** a toast can be swiped right, off the screen's edge. Let go early,
  it settles back.
- **Stillness:** a toast that takes the place of one with the same mark does not
  replay its icon.
- **Cast shadow:** off by default; `shadow` turns it on. Only the front casts in
  a closed deck, and every card does in the open list.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
A notification is there at once and gone at once, with no growth, fold or fade.
An inline notification's place opens and closes at once, and so does a change of
height. An update shows the new words on the same frame the old ones go. The
status mark is simply there, with no beat. In a stack, the deck's fades and
resizes run on the reduced clock, with no travel and no deal, and a swipe does
not follow the pointer.

V12/NotificationsPanel.title: NotificationsPanel
V12/NotificationsPanel.summary:
Carbon for IBM Products' notifications panel, prop for prop: a floating panel
from the header's bell, its notifications grouped into Today, Yesterday and
Previous. Each row has a status mark, when it came, a title, a description with
Read more past two lines, and a link. Unread rows carry a blue dot cut out of
the mark, and a semibold title. The header holds Dismiss all, Do not disturb and
settings; View all is the foot. The host owns `open` and `data`. A press
outside, not on the trigger, or Escape calls `onClickOutside`, and Escape puts
focus back on the trigger. `NotificationsBell` is the trigger's icon: pass it
the panel's Do not disturb state, and the same state back as
`doNotDisturbDefaultToggled`, so the panel opens as it was left.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Open:** the floating snap from its trigger, timed by size. The frame grows
  from the trigger while the content moves down with the opening, landing just
  after the frame.
- **Close:** the far edge pulls back into the trigger. Reopened mid-exit, it
  turns round.
- **Dismiss:** a dismissed row's place shuts, one step faster as an exit, while
  its content holds still and the soft edge closes over it, with no fade. What
  is below closes up with it in one move. A group's title goes with its last
  row.
- **Dismiss all:** the titles and rows leave on a stagger faster than the
  entrance, each rising 8px and fading out. Then the list resizes to the empty
  state, which comes in after it.
- **Arrive:** a notification added while the panel is open opens its place on
  its travel's step under the soft edge. Its content comes down 8px into it from
  half the open over `fast-02`, with no fade. Its status mark plays its beat
  once it has landed.
- **Read more:** the description's place opens on its travel's step and shuts
  one step faster, under the soft edge. Its lines are already there, so the text
  is uncovered in place. The clamp comes back once the place has closed. The
  label rolls, and the chevron turns.
- **Do not disturb:** the header's toggle and the bell slash on the icon's own
  motion. Turned on, the pip goes and the slash draws in. Turned off, the slash
  retracts and the bell rings, then the pip is back. Arrivals keep coming.
- **View all:** the whole footer cell takes the ghost Button's rollover. Its
  count rolls.
- **Rollover:** a row that is a control (`onNotificationClick`), Read more and
  the link take the kit's rollover.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The panel fades in place. Places open and close at once. Dismiss all and an
arrival's content are fades on the reduced clock, with no travel. The bell's
drawings change at once, and Read more's label swaps in place.

V12/NumberInput.title: NumberInput
V12/NumberInput.summary:
A field for a number, with − and + steppers inset at its trailing edge. It is
the text input's field: its label, outline, status mark and one message line. On
a step the number rolls to its next value. `NumberInput` takes Carbon's props,
plus `corners`, `frame`, `variant`, `lateErrors`, `typingPauseMs`,
`messagePlacement`, `statusBeat`, `timeScale` and the AI fill state.
`type="text"` parses and formats the number for a locale. `NumberInputSkeleton`
is the field while its value loads.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Roll:** a step rolls the number to its next value: up as it rises, down as
  it falls, only the digits that change. It runs on moderate-01 with
  standard-productive; a roll that interrupts one already moving carries on at
  speed. A step is a stepper, ↑ or ↓ in the field, or a `value` set from outside
  that isn't the one the field reported. The roll sits over the input's own
  text, which stays a real input. Typing never rolls, and neither does a step
  held at a bound.
- **Outline ladder:** the text input's. Hover, press and focus step the outline.
- **Error border:** an error settles in once, with the text input's border.
- **Message line:** helper, warning and error share one line and swap in place,
  out then in.
- **Status mark:** the warning or error mark sits before the steppers and swaps
  as the status changes. `statusBeat` plays its icon once as it arrives.
- **Late status:** an error that rises while typing, a number out of range say,
  waits for a pause (`typingPauseMs`, default 1000ms) or blur. One that falls
  shows on the keystroke. `lateErrors={false}` shows every status at once.
- **Rollover:** the steppers are ghost icon buttons, with the rollover's press
  shrink and no hover expand. Each icon plays on its button's hover.
- **Tooltip:** the two steppers share one tooltip. Moving from − to + puts it
  there at once, with its text changing in place.
- **AI fill:** a fill and a revert swap the value; they never roll.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The number changes at once, with no roll. The outline and the error border
change on half of fast-01. The message line, the status mark, the steppers'
release, the tooltip and an AI fill change at once. A rising status still waits
for the pause or blur.

V12/OptionsTile.title: Options tile
V12/OptionsTile.summary:
A tile for one group of settings. The heading is a button that holds the
chevron, the title and a one-line `summary` of what the settings are set to.
`enabled` adds a switch over the heading's end that turns the group on or off;
`onChange` hears it. The body opens to show the settings, its children. Without
children the tile doesn't open, and the heading is plain text. `invalid`, `warn`
and `locked` put a status, with its text, in the summary's place, in that order.
Open, the summary goes, but a status stays. Locked makes the switch read-only.
`open` is the initial state, followed whenever it changes, and `onToggle` hears
each toggle. `size` sets the heading: lg 48px (default) or xl 64px.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
The body is the shared disclosure.

- **Open and shut:** the body opens as the summary's line shuts, as one swap on
  one clock: the step of the longer travel, on standard-productive. Shutting,
  the line opens as the body shuts. Tiles that change in one commit move as one
  motion.
- **Settings in:** opening, the settings come down 8px from the opening's first
  frame, over one duration token longer than the opening.
- **Sheet:** open, a hairline sits atop the body and holds still. The body's
  sheet runs to the tile's bottom over the heading's lower part. It fades in and
  out at the motion's ends. The heading's lower corners follow the body on its
  clock and curve, so they never snap.
- **Summary fade:** the summary only fades, in place, over fast-01. Opening, it
  is gone before anything moves over it. Shutting, it comes back once the
  heading has landed.
- **Summary words:** new words swap out, then in. They swap in place, or, when
  the switch changed them, 8px the way the knob went.
- **Rollover:** the tiles' quiet rollover on the heading, flush, with no growth
  past the tile and no press shrink. With a switch, the heading shows a ring
  instead of a fill.
- **Switch:** the kit's Toggle, with its own glide.
- **Chevron:** down when shut, up when open. The heading is its motion icon
  frame.

`timeScale` multiplies the disclosure, the rollover, the summary swap and the
switch.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The disclosure opens and shuts at once, and the settings fade in on the reduced
clock. The summary changes at once, and its swap is a snap. The switch fades
rather than glides.

V12/PageHeader.title: Page header
V12/PageHeader.summary:
The top of a page: a breadcrumb, a title, a subtitle, `children`, tags, page
actions, an action bar and tabs (`navigation`). It sticks to the top of its
scroll container, `pageHeaderOffset` below it. Past 16px of scroll it collapses
to one 48px row of the breadcrumb, the title, the page actions and the action
bar, then the tabs. Back at the top it expands. `collapseHeader` holds it
collapsed, and `hasCollapseHeaderToggle` adds a button for it. Its layout
follows its own width, not the window's. Below 672px the page actions go under
the title, and the collapsed row has no breadcrumb. Each row is split 60/40
between the title or breadcrumb and the actions from 672px up, and 75/25 below.
Page actions given as descriptions fold as a set into a "Page actions" menu
button when they don't fit; a node of your own stays as it is. The action bar
gives its trailing items to an overflow menu. The title truncates on one line,
with its full text in a tooltip. Its controls sit one size down from the density
around it. `frame="flush"`, the default, is the quiet surface and its hairline;
`ghost` paints the ground it sits on, with no hairline. `corners="rounded"`
rounds it in the page or in a card.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Collapse and expand:** one layout transaction. The header's height leads,
  and the breadcrumb and the tabs move from where they were to where they land,
  on its clock. The clock is the step for the farthest travel, one step faster
  collapsing, on standard-productive.
- **Title swap:** the title doesn't travel. Two copies swap in place, out then
  in. Collapsing, the large title rolls up a line and away through a soft edge,
  then the compact one rolls up into place from a line below, landing with the
  header. Expanding is the mirror. The breadcrumb's last slash comes and goes on
  the same beats.
- **Details:** the subtitle, `children` and the tags fade in place on the
  title's beats, out collapsing and in expanding. The edge that moves with the
  header cuts them where it ends.
- **The jump:** every button that changes place jumps: into or out of a menu
  button, between its rows and the collapsed row, and on a resize. Copies of the
  leaving buttons shrink out 4px, opaque, over the first third of the clock.
  Then the arriving ones grow in from 4px small over the rest. In a collapse or
  expand the clock is the move's; on a resize it is fast-01. A button within 4px
  of its old place stays put.
- **Ghost hairline:** with `frame="ghost"`, the collapsed row's hairline fades
  in on fast-00 as the compact title lands, and out as the large one starts
  back.
- **Soft edge:** content scrolling under the header leaves into a soft edge at
  its bottom, which grows over the first 16px of content under it.
- **The room it keeps:** collapsing on the scroll, it keeps the room it gives up
  as a margin below, moving with its height. Nothing below moves, the page's
  height doesn't change, and a short page collapses too. A collapse from
  `collapseHeader` or the toggle keeps no room: the content follows the header.
- **No fade:** with `motion={{ fade: false }}`, the titles roll through a hard
  edge, the edge over the details is hard, and the slash comes and goes on its
  beats with no fade.
- **Interruption:** a turn mid-move goes on from where everything is. An edge
  the scroll crosses mid-move is answered when the move lands. A resize across
  672px changes the layout at once.
- `timeScale` multiplies the clock.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
It collapses and expands at once, and the buttons don't jump. On the scroll it
still keeps the room it gives up.

V12/Pagination.title: Pagination
V12/Pagination.summary:
The footer of a long list or a data table. On the start side are the page size
select and the item range. On the end side are the page select, the page count,
and back and forward buttons. It takes Carbon's props: `page` (from 1),
`pageSize`, `pageSizes`, `totalItems`, `pagesUnknown`, `isLastPage`, the text
props, `disabled`, `size` and `onChange`. The selects are the kit's inline
Dropdown, one size down from the bar. The buttons are the kit's ghost
IconButtons. A new page size goes back to page 1. Reaching the last page moves
focus to the back button; reaching the first moves it to the forward button. A
bar narrower than its controls scrolls sideways in the kit's Scroller.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Content swap:** only what changes with the page swaps, out then in. The
  range's "11–20" swaps along x, in the page's direction. The page number swaps
  along y: forward, the old number leaves upward and the new one comes up from
  below; back, the other way. The old text moves 8px and fades on fast-01,
  exit-productive. Then the new one comes in from the other side on fast-02,
  entrance-productive. A change with the page unmoved, such as a new page size,
  comes from the end side. The first text is simply there.
- **Glide:** the rest of the range text, "of 103 items", is not swapped. It
  moves from its old place to its new one on the swap's clock, on
  standard-productive. In right to left it moves the other way.
- **Page count:** "of 11 pages" changes at once. It follows the page size, not
  the page.
- **Lists:** the page size and page lists are the Dropdown's, on the Menu's
  surface.
- **Rollover:** the selects and the buttons are full round. An icon-only
  button's hover is a circle.
- **Tooltips:** the back and forward buttons share one `TooltipGroup`.
- **Slow motion:** `timeScale` slows the lists, the swap and the scroller.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The swap is a snap: the new text is there on one frame, with no fade, and the
rest of the text is there at once. The lists and the rollover change at once.
Tooltips show and leave at once.

V12/PaginationNav.title: PaginationNav
V12/PaginationNav.summary:
Page numbers between a back and a forward button. The first and last pages
always show. Between them is a window of numbers, and the pages hidden on each
side sit behind a "…" that opens a list of them. It takes Carbon's props: `page`
(from 0), `totalItems` (the number of pages), `itemsShown` (default 10, at least
4), `loop`, `disableOverflow`, `size` (default lg), `tooltipAlignment`,
`tooltipPosition`, `translateWithId` and `onChange(index)`. `variant` sets the
marker's color: `inverse`, the default, or `hero`, the brand blue. `motion`
takes the selection kit's dials; keys left out take the kit's. `onMove` is
called as each glide of the marker starts.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Selection marker:** the current page's mark is an underline at the row's
  foot, as line tabs draw it. It glides from page to page, timed by travel, its
  leading edge ahead. The page label takes its selected weight, 600, and color
  where the marker covers it.
- **Selection gesture:** a press on a page reaches the marker toward it. The
  release picks it.
- **Window shift:** when the window of numbers shifts, the row reflows as one
  strip. The numbers that stay slide to their new places, timed by travel. The
  marker moves on the strip's clock, so a step that shifts the window by one
  leaves it still while the numbers pass under it.
- **List reflow, carry:** a number leaving slides on with the strip and fades
  out, faster. A number arriving slides in and fades up.
- **Soft edge:** the window's numbers sit between soft edges, 16px at most and
  never wider than the room to the next icon box. A number travelling out is
  gone before it reaches a "…". One arriving where a "…" went waits until it has
  gone.
- **Overflow list:** the "…" opens the kit's floating listbox of the hidden
  pages, the Dropdown's, on the Menu's surface. It snaps from the press and
  folds back into it. It shows five and a half rows and scrolls.
- **Rollover:** the numbers and the "…" take the kit's rollover, full round: a
  circle, or a pill on a long number. Hover adds a glow and the label steps
  brighter. The press insets 1px and stays round while the marker reaches toward
  it.
- **Tooltips:** the back and forward buttons are the kit's ghost IconButtons, in
  one `TooltipGroup`.
- **Keyboard:** the "…", closed: ↓, Enter or Space open the list on the first
  page, ↑ on the last; Home and End too. Open: ↑ and ↓ move, without wrapping;
  Home and End; Page Up and Page Down move 10; digits find a page; Enter or
  Space choose; Escape and Tab close. The current page has
  `aria-current="page"`. A polite live region says "Page n of N".

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Nothing travels. The marker fades across to the new page, on a shorter clock.
The numbers land at once; leaving and arriving ones fade, on a shorter clock.
The overflow list is there or gone at once. The rollover changes at once.
Tooltips show and leave at once.

V12/Popover.title: Popover
V12/Popover.summary:
A surface opened from a trigger, for content that is not a list of actions:
filters, settings, a short form. `Popover` and `PopoverContent` take Carbon's
props. With `anchor`, the popover is a portalled panel opened from that element
instead. There is no caret: the surface sits 4px off its trigger. The content
has no padding of its own; the host pads it.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Open:** the frame grows from its cause, as geometry: the press on the
  trigger, else the trigger's center. The content slides out of it on y and
  never scales. Opened from the start, with no gesture, it is there with no
  motion.
- **Close:** the far edge folds back toward the cause. The surface is gone on
  the fold's last frame.
- **Fade:** it fades up over the first part of the open and out over the last
  part of the close: 40ms on a clock of 220ms or less, else 80ms.
  `exitFade={false}` folds back opaque.
- **Interrupted:** reopened while it leaves, it turns round from where it is.
- **Soft edge:** on every side where the container clips the content,
  `min(16px, h, H − h)` per side, from the snap's live geometry. Only the
  content is masked, and there is no mask at rest.
- **Timing by size:** a large popover, such as a form, opens and closes on the
  slower surface clock.
- **Cast shadow:** off by default. `shadow` or `dropShadow` turns it on; it
  follows the surface on every frame.
- **While open:** scrolling and resizing place it again once a frame, with no
  motion.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text: There at once and gone at once: no growth, slide, fade or soft edge.

V12/Processing.title: Processing
V12/Processing.summary:
The working mark for a turn or a job: three dots that load in and pulse on the
loading clock, turn into a triangle while the machine acts and a square while it
waits on a person, and shrink out.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
| Pattern             | Where                           | Values                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Load-in             | On mount, or any mode after out | Each dot grows in over slow-01, fast-02 apart, entrance-expressive, joining the running pulse at once                                                             |
| Pulse               | Every formation                 | In sets, dots 250ms apart; each swells 225ms, entrance-expressive, and settles 600ms, standard-productive; then 175ms quiet. A set is 1500ms, the square's 1750ms |
| Swing               | A change of mode                | One clockwise swing on arcs, 150° into a shape, at least 90° into the line; dots fast-00 apart, longest arc first, standard-productive                            |
| Swing clock         | By the longest arc              | Under 8 units moderate-03, under 12 slow-01, under 16 slow-02, else slow-03; the same time at every size                                                          |
| Spin                | Triangle, square                | One revolution in 8 loading periods, clockwise                                                                                                                    |
| Square's fourth dot | Into the square                 | Grows in as the others swing; into or out of the square the dots finish their set first                                                                           |
| Wiggle              | The handle, any formation       | Each dot bobs over slow-01, moderate-02 apart, standard-expressive: 6 units up from the line, 3 out from a shape's centre                                         |
| Out                 | `out`, or the handle            | Each dot shrinks over fast-01, fast-00 apart, exit-expressive                                                                                                     |
| Shared clock        | Every mark on a page            | Pulse and spin read one page clock, so marks pulse and turn together; off screen they hold                                                                        |
| Interruption        | A request mid-swing             | Swings on clockwise from where the dots are, never back; out interrupts at once                                                                                   |
| Reduced motion      | Every change                    | Each mode's still picture; out hides the dots at once; the wiggle does nothing                                                                                    |

V12/ProgressBar.title: ProgressBar
V12/ProgressBar.summary:
An amount of work as a line, with Carbon's props: a label, the bar, helper text
and a status mark at the bar's end. With no `value` it is indeterminate. It adds
`variant` (neutral or hero), `pulse`, `mark` and `motion`.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Fill:** travels from where it is to the new value on standard-productive,
  its clock from the distance. The fill's line grows 1px from 15% to 85% of the
  work, in the same tween.
- **Burst:** at most one new tween per `fast-02`. An update inside that window
  retargets the running tween from the fill's place and speed.
- **Loop:** with no value, a segment up to 40% of the track crosses it, one pass
  per loading period, on standard-productive. Every bar on a page is in one
  phase.
- **Loop and value:** a value picks up from the segment's live edges. A fill
  that loses its value leaves toward the end, a step faster, and the loop joins
  at the next pass.
- **Finished:** the fill travels to the end; once it lands, the bar takes the
  success colour and the check swaps in, then plays once.
- **Error:** the error colour at once, and the fill stays where it failed. With
  no value, the segment leaves toward the end.
- **Status colour:** crossfades on `fast-02`, linear.
- **Status mark:** swaps in place, out then in.
- **Pulse:** `pulse`, while active with a value: a highlight crosses the filled
  part to the leading edge, one pass every two loading periods. It never passes
  the leading edge.
- **Right to left:** the bar is mirrored, so the fill, the segment and the pulse
  run from the right.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The fill is at its value at once. With no value, three short still segments
stand in for the loop. No pulse. The status mark snaps in, with no beat, and the
status colour crossfades on half the clock.

V12/ProgressIndicator.title: ProgressIndicator
V12/ProgressIndicator.summary:
A task's steps on a line, drawn as line tabs. Its props are Carbon's
`ProgressIndicator` and `ProgressStep`, plus `reach` from `useProgressReach`.
Each step has an icon, a label and an optional secondary label. The current step
carries a bar on the line, and a fill runs over the complete steps.
`ProgressIndicatorSkeleton` draws it loading.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Bar:** the selection's bar glides to the current step by travel, its leading
  edge ahead by a stretch that scales with the track.
- **Reach:** a press that will move the bar, on a step or on Back and Next
  through `useProgressReach`, leans it toward that step. A press let go
  elsewhere reaches back.
- **Line:** one fill to the current step, on the bar's clock, so the two land
  together. Without a bar move, on its own travel's duration.
- **Icons:** each step's icon changes to its new state in place.
- **Rollover:** a step you can choose takes the press shrink.
- **Layout:** a resize or a change of direction places the bar and the line at
  once.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
No travel and no reach: the bar fades across to the new step. The line and the
icons are there at once.

V12/ProgressRing.title: ProgressRing
V12/ProgressRing.summary:
An amount of work as a ring, for small places such as a file chip, a row or an
uploader item. It is the Spinner's sibling, with ProgressBar's prop names: the
loud arc over the Spinner's quiet base, a label and helper text. It comes in the
Spinner's sizes, 16, 20, 24 and 32px, neutral or hero. With no `value` it is the
Spinner.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Draw-on:** with a value, as it mounts or takes another mark's place, the arc
  draws on from 12 o'clock, clockwise, as the track fades up. It runs on
  entrance-productive, its clock from the arc's travel, never under
  `moderate-01`.
- **Value:** the arc's end travels from where it is to the new value on
  standard-productive, its clock from the distance. The line grows with it, from
  its rest width at 15% to twice it at 85%, in the same tween. The outer edge
  holds, so the line grows inward.
- **Burst:** at most one new tween per `fast-02`. An update inside that window
  retargets the running tween from where the arc is.
- **Hand-off from turning:** a value that arrives while the Spinner turns is one
  move. The turn slows so the arc's tail lands at 12 o'clock while its length
  eases to the value. It leaves at the Spinner's own speed, so it never stops
  and restarts.
- **Finished:** the arc completes the ring. Then the status hand-off, out then
  in, with no fades: the ring shrinks 4px on `fast-01`, the success disc grows
  from 4px under its size on `fast-02`, and its check draws on, `fast-02`.
- **Error:** with a value, the arc turns red where it failed, finishes its
  travel there, then hands off to the error disc. With no value, the whole
  Spinner, its base too, turns red as it shrinks.
- **Back to active:** from a mark, the mark fades out on `fast-02`, then the
  ring or the Spinner draws on.
- **Value removed:** the ring closes, its tail catching its head, as the track
  fades, on `fast-02`. Then the Spinner draws on.
- **Right to left:** the arc runs counter-clockwise.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Values land at once, with no draw. The hand-off, the close and the marks are
there at once. With no value, the Spinner's three still dots stand in for the
turn.

V12/Props.title: Prop vocabulary
V12/Props.summary:
One name for each idea across the v12 components. Carbon v11's names stay where
v11 has them and they fit (`size`, `type` on Tag, `labelText`, `lowContrast`,
`invalidText` …).

**No aliases:** one name per concept for v12, including v11 names that break the
system (Tabs' `contained`, Button's `tertiary` and `ghost` kinds). The earlier
names are gone, not accepted; the migration table lists each one.

The shared types and the resolutions that are more than `a ?? b` are in
`props.ts`, with tests beside it (`props.test.ts`).

sections.title: motion
sections.text:
_One tuning pattern._

A component's tuning (the numbers a review dials: a segment's share, a swing, a
band's width, a pass's period) is **one `motion` object prop**,
`Partial<…Motion>`: each key left out is the component's shipped number. Never
top-level props, and never a store a product calls.

| Component                                                         | `motion`                                            | Keys                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The selection family, Menu and its buttons, Slider, PaginationNav | `Partial<SelectionMotion>`, `Partial<MenuMotion>` … | their clocks, and `timeScale` (above)                                                                                                                                                 |
| Spinner, ProgressRing                                             | `Partial<SpinnerMotion>`                            | `arc`, `swing`, `swingPeriods`, `gapSmall`, `gapLarge`, `gapStyle`, `strokeScale`, `strokeMax`, `enterScale`, `enter` (the scale-in's scale and its shortest clock, a duration token) |
| ProgressBar                                                       | `Partial<ProgressBarMotion>`                        | `segment`, `pulsePeriods`                                                                                                                                                             |
| ShimmerText                                                       | `Partial<ShimmerTextMotion>`                        | `shortSpeed`, `longSpeed`, `restMs` (the length rule: the speed by the words' length, then one rest; it replaces `speed` and `periods`), `band`, `weight`, `weightAt`                 |
| PageHeader                                                        | `Partial<PageHeaderMotion>` (`PAGE_HEADER_MOTION`)  | `fade` (default true: the collapse's soft edges and the slash's fade; false, hard edges, opaque to the last frame)                                                                    |

- **Where every instance should follow, a lab-only global store** besides the
  prop: the spinner's `setSpinnerMotion` (`resetSpinnerMotion`,
  `useSpinnerMotion`), which writes `SPINNER_MOTION` and redraws every Spinner
  and ProgressRing on the page, so the Loading page's Tuning dials busy buttons,
  InlineLoading and the uploader at once. It is for the lab; an instance's own
  `motion` wins for the keys it sets.
- A lab keeps its draft itself (the spinner's in `localStorage`); the kit stores
  nothing.
- Processing has no tuning props (its clocks are the loading clock's and the
  tokens'), so it has no `motion`.
- **DataTableReveal's `stagger` and `staggerCap`** are top-level, as
  `SkeletonReveal`'s options are: `stagger`, how far apart the arriving rows
  fade in, ms (default `LOADING_MOTION.rowStaggerMs`, 30); `staggerCap`, where
  that stagger stops growing, ms (default `LOADING_MOTION.staggerCapMs`,
  `moderate-02`, 220; `Infinity` for none). They are tuning by the rule above,
  so they would move into a `motion` object; that is not done yet.

V12/RadioButton.title: RadioButton
V12/RadioButton.summary:
A circle for choosing one option from a group. `RadioButton` and
`RadioButtonGroup` take Carbon's props, plus `timeScale`. The group holds the
choice, its legend and one message line; it is in a row by default. `RadioMark`
is the circle and dot alone, for a control that draws a radio it doesn't own.
`RadioButtonSkeleton` is the radio button while it loads.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Dot in:** the fill changes at once. 40ms later the 6px dot grows from its
  center, half size to full, on fast-02 with entrance-productive. The state
  reads first.
- **Dot out:** the dot shrinks and fades on fast-01 with exit-productive.
- **Hover:** the rollover on the circle. Off, a wash of the text color at 8%;
  on, a toned step of the fill. The glow fades in on fast-02 and out on fast-01.
  The circle grows 1px. Hovering the label plays it too, however the label
  wraps.
- **Press:** no press color of its own. The circle presses 1px in.
- **Status ring:** `invalid` and `warn` color the circle's stroke and add 1px
  outside it, red or yellow. The rollover paints the ring, so it grows with the
  hover. A group's status rings every button in it. Disabled and read-only show
  no status.
- **Message line:** helper, warning and error share one line and swap in place,
  out then in.
- **Keyboard:** a native radio group. One tab stop; the arrow keys move the
  choice and wrap, and the dots follow. Read-only changes nothing.
- **Focus:** keyboard only, 2px `$text-primary`, 2px outside the circle; 3px out
  while a status shows. It has no transition.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The dot appears and leaves at once. The hover changes at once. The press still
shows; the release and the return to hover are at once. The message line changes
at once.

V12/ReasoningTrace.title: ReasoningTrace
V12/ReasoningTrace.summary:
> **Problem statement:** while an agent works, a person needs to see that it is
> working, what it is doing now, and afterwards what it did and how long it
> took, without the transcript turning into a log. Carbon has no equivalent:
> `Accordion` is a disclosure but not a status, `InlineLoading` is a status but
> holds no steps, and `@carbon/ai-chat`'s reasoning steps are part of a whole
> chat application. ReasoningTrace is the disclosure alone, standalone React: a
> header that says what happened and how long it took, and, when open, the steps
> (ReasoningStep) or the code it ran (CodeSnippet).

It replaces the library's earlier Trajectory and labs's `Processing` for v12.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text:

It replaces the library's earlier Trajectory and labs's `Processing` for v12.

sections.title: Anatomy
sections.text:
- **Header** — one button: the thinking animation while it thinks, the label
  ("Thinking", "Complete", "Running", "Used tool"), an optional subject as
  `InlineCode`, the duration, and the chevron.
- **Card** — ReasoningSteps, joined by square rules; the card rounds the whole
  at `$border-radius-08`. Content that is not a step list brings its own card.
- **Footer** — "View plan details" (or "Planning…" while it runs) opens the full
  trace in the PlanCanvas pattern. It is a button that reads as a link, with
  `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` for the region it opens.

sections.title: Behaviour
sections.text:
- **Opens and closes** on Carbon's disclosure motion (`moderate-01`; entrance
  easing in, exit out). Closed content leaves the tab order.
- **Resolves flush.** Once `status` is `complete` the animation leaves and the
  header sits flush, with no icon. The change is announced politely.
- **The live step** is primary text with Carbon's small `Loading`, so it reads
  as live rather than disabled. A failed step says "Failed" as well as showing
  `ErrorFilled`.

sections.title: The thinking animation
sections.text:
`ThinkingIndicator` is the processing animation from Carbon2027 - Modelling:
three dots settle, ripple, a darker square passes along them, they collapse to a
point and spread again. One cycle is four `slow-02` durations (2.8s; the source
video measured 2.6s), on Carbon's standard productive easing. Dots are
`$interactive`; the square is `$link-primary-hover`. It is decorative, and it
holds still under reduced motion.

sections.title: Getting started

V12/RecipeRenderer.title: Recipes
V12/RecipeRenderer.summary:
> **Problem statement:** a layout, a flow or a small widget built from Carbon
> components is today either prose in a guideline or code someone copies. A
> **recipe** is the same composition written as data, so a person can preview it
> here, a tool can check it, and an agent can assemble a screen from it without
> anyone writing freeform UI.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text:
> **Problem statement:** a layout, a flow or a small widget built from Carbon
> components is today either prose in a guideline or code someone copies. A
> **recipe** is the same composition written as data, so a person can preview it
> here, a tool can check it, and an agent can assemble a screen from it without
> anyone writing freeform UI.

sections.title: What a recipe is
sections.text:
A JSON file in `recipes/<name>.recipe.json`, held to `recipe.schema.json`:

- **Real components only.** Each node names `"<package>:<Export>"` —
  `@carbon/react` or a labs v12 package — and is rendered from an explicit
  registry. A recipe adds no component and no styling of its own.
- **Carbon's grid.** `grid.span` places a node in a Carbon `Column` of its
  parent `Grid`.
- **Carbon's spacing.** `gap` and `padding` are spacing token names
  (`"spacing-05"`), never values. `gap` is rendered by Carbon's `Stack`.
- **No literals.** No `style`, no `className`, no px, rem, hex or colour
  function anywhere in props.
- **Selectable.** `meta` carries `intent`, `useWhen` and `preferInstead`, the
  same fields a component's metadata uses, so a recipe is chosen by what it is
  for and stopped by what is better.

A **flow** is a list of steps, each a screen and the events that leave it:
`{ "$event": "next" }` in a prop raises `next`, and the step's `on.next` names
where it goes. Only the current step is rendered, and focus moves with it.

sections.title: The recipes here
sections.text:
- **settings-page** (layout): one form, the lead, on the grid.
- **create-topic** (flow): the three steps of Carbon's `CreateFullPage` example
  (`packages/react/src/examples/CreateFullPage`, carbon#23309), plus the two
  places it can end.
- **status-tile** (widget): one resource's health and the way to its detail.

sections.title: What a recipe cannot do yet
sections.text:
- Hold state between controls (validation, a field that enables another).
- Load data, or show a loading or error state that depends on a request.
- Pass an icon or any other component as a prop value.
- Align a child to the start of a gap. Carbon's `Stack` stretches every child to
  its column, and has no align prop: the tags in status-tile show it.

Each is a design question before it is a schema field.

sections.title: Checking a recipe
sections.text:
`recipe-lint` (in the Carbon Design Harness) validates the schema, resolves
every component against the installed `@carbon/react` and labs packages, checks
spacing tokens against `@carbon/layout`, walks every flow for unreachable steps
and dead events, and refuses literals.

sections.title: Where this goes
sections.text:
Recipes are published with this package, so they reach npm, and later the Carbon
MCP, from one place. Whether the renderer itself should ever move into
`@carbon/react`, and whether the schema becomes a Carbon format, are open
questions for the Carbon maintainers.

V12/Recipes.title: Recipes
V12/Recipes.summary:
Screens put together from the parts, each for one job. A recipe fills its
regions with the parts a team passes it and owns the rest: the frame, the
states and the motion between them.

sections.title: Assistant
sections.text:
An assistant beside the page: ask in words, see the reply's work as it
happens, and keep the page in view. `Assistant` is a `ChatPane` beside the
page holding a `ChatShell`: the header with the questions' navigator and
Close, the conversation, the prompt with its file chips and add menu, and
suggestions under the prompt until the conversation starts. Avoid it for a
single action with fixed inputs (use a form or a modal) or for help text (use
a toggletip).

The pane opens its own space, the page narrowing on every frame of it. Send
swaps to Stop; the reply's status row arrives, its steps joining under it,
then its words. Closed from inside the pane, focus goes back to where it was
when the pane opened, or to the page's launcher (`launcherButtonRef`).

sections.title: Resource index
sections.text:
Find, filter and act on many items of one kind. `ResourceIndex` puts the app
shell round the screen: `header`, `nav`, and in the workspace the
`pageHeader`, the `toolbar` row, the `filters` in use, `main`, the `batch` bar
while rows are selected, the `footer`, and the `panel` of filters. `state`
sets what the regions show: `loading`, `first-use`, `loaded`,
`filtered-empty`, `batch`, `panel-open` or `error`. Use it for roughly 10 or
more items that people search, filter and act on together; avoid it for a
handful (use a list) or for one item (use a details page).

A change of what main shows is a content swap, out then in. Loading to loaded
is the table's own reveal, and the footer arrives with the table's last row.
An empty state replaces the table whole, footer included.
`ResourceIndexScreen` is the screen without the shell, for a shell of your
own.

sections.title: Create flow
sections.text:
Create one item that needs a few groups of settings, in order, with a review
before it is made. `CreateFlow` is a tearsheet holding a step flow: the steps
in a column beside the form, the current step in the main area, and Cancel,
Back and Next (the submit words on the last step) in the footer. Each open
starts on the first step; the values are the caller's. Avoid it for a handful
of fields (use a modal).

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Each recipe's parts keep their own reduced forms. The assistant's pane fades
in and out. A create flow's steps snap, and its tearsheet fades.

V12/RollText.title: RollText
V12/RollText.summary:
A short text that rolls to its next value, like a counter: only the characters
that change move. For a value that steps through a list, such as a slider's
step, a status word or a count's label.

The rules for when to use it are below; the mechanics (what stays, what rolls,
the clip, the blur) are in the header of `RollText.tsx`.

V12/Scroller.title: Scroller
V12/Scroller.summary:
A floating pill per axis in place of the native scrollbar, over native scrolling
on a container or the window. The pill reads out where you are, and you can drag
it or press beside it. Wheel, trackpad, touch and keys scroll natively. Size the
root like any box; the viewport inside fills it and scrolls. `WindowScroller`
puts the pill on the window's edge and hides the page's own scrollbar while it
is mounted. The rest color is `$border-strong`, so it steps with the layer.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Readout:** the pill's offset follows the scroll 1:1, never eased. Its length
  is the viewport's share of the content, at least 32px.
- **Length:** a change in the content's size glides the length over fast-02, on
  standard-productive. A change in the viewport's size follows at once.
- **Arrival:** scrolling, the pointer near the edge, or keyboard focus brings
  the pill in: a fade over fast-01, linear, while its thickness grows from 90%
  over fast-02, on entrance-productive. A run of activity never replays it.
- **Leave:** 1000ms after the last activity it fades over fast-02, on
  exit-productive. Never while it is hovered, pressed, dragged or focused.
- **Hover:** a 16px strip along the edge thickens the pill from 4 to 6px about
  its center line, fast-02 in and fast-01 out, with the hover color step.
- **Press:** the pill insets 0.5px on every side, with the pressed color step,
  held while dragging.
- **Squash:** dragged past either end, the far end comes toward the wall, up to
  4px, and springs back over fast-01 on release.
- **Track press:** a press beside the pill scrolls a page (87.5% of the
  viewport) toward it, or jumps to the press. The duration follows the pill's
  travel, 40 to 150ms, on standard-productive. A wheel, touch, key, drag or
  another press stops it where it is.
- **Soft edge:** a side of the viewport is masked only while content is past it,
  `min(16px, half the viewport, the amount past)`. None at rest at the top, and
  none where something is stuck to that side.
- **Corner:** with both axes, each track stops short of the corner by the other
  pill's hover footprint and the inset.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
Fades only, on the reduced clock. The thickness does not grow, the length does
not glide and the squash does not spring back. A track press jumps.

V12/Search.title: Search
V12/Search.summary:
Carbon's Search on the text input's field: a magnifier at the start, the input,
and a clear button at the end. `labelText` is hidden and names the search
landmark. The clear button, or Escape with a value, empties the field, calls
`onChange` and `onClear`, and puts focus back in the input. It does not show
when disabled or read-only. `ExpandableSearch` is its magnifier button until
pressed, then grows into the field and takes focus. Emptied and left, or on
Escape in an empty field, it closes back into the button; `isExpanded` holds it
open. Its open width is `100%`, or `--cds-search-expanded-inline-size`.
`SearchSkeleton` is the search while it loads.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Expand:** an expandable search grows from its button's box to its full
  width, and closes back into it. The clock follows the travel: under 24px
  fast-02, under 120px moderate-01, under 480px moderate-02. It opens on
  entrance-productive and closes one step faster, on exit-productive. The width
  moves as one layout change, so what sits beside it moves on the same clock. A
  turn mid-move takes the step of what is left.
- **Content with the opening:** shut, the content waits 8px back toward the
  button. Opening from shut, it starts at half the clock and comes into place
  over fast-02, on entrance-productive. It is laid out at its open width
  throughout, so its text never reflows. Closing, it holds still. Reopened while
  closing, it resumes from where it is.
- **Soft edge:** while it moves, the trailing edge fades over up to 16px, so
  nothing pops as it lands.
- **Fill and hairline:** opening, the field's fill and hairline fade in on
  fast-02. Closing, they fade out on fast-01 once it has closed.
- **Clear button in:** the first typed character brings it in as the snap's
  mark: from half size, opaque, growing about its center on fast-02, on
  entrance-productive. It keeps its place while hidden, so the text never
  reflows. Typing never moves it.
- **Clear button out:** emptied, it leaves one step faster, on fast-01 and
  exit-productive, back to half size and fading.
- **Hover:** the field is the magnifier's icon frame. Hovering anywhere on it
  plays the magnifier's hover. Not while disabled or read-only.
- **Rollover:** the magnifier button and the clear button take the press shrink,
  never the hover expand.
- **Outline ladder:** the text input's: hover, press and focus on the outline. A
  press on a focused field holds its focus edge.

The clocks are read from the token variables where the search is, so a page's
slow motion reaches them.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
No travel and no scale. An expandable search opens or shuts at once, and its
content fades in on fast-02 at half the clock. The clear button only fades, on
the reduced clock. The fill, the outline and the magnifier's color change on
fast-01 at half the clock.

V12/Select.title: Select
V12/Select.summary:
Carbon's Select, a native `<select>`, on the kit's text field: a label, the
field with a chevron and a status mark at its trailing edge, and one message
line. `Select` takes Carbon's props, and its options are `SelectItem` and
`SelectItemGroup`. The select fills the field, so a press anywhere on it opens
the list. Where the browser lets the page style the list, it is drawn in the
page with the Dropdown's look; elsewhere it is the platform's own. Read-only
takes focus but never opens. `inline` puts the label beside a quiet field.
`SelectSkeleton` is the select while its value loads.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Outline ladder:** the text input's. Hover moves the hairline a step, a press
  steps it further, and focus is the accent at 2px. The fill never changes.
- **Error border:** an error settles in once.
- **Message line:** helper text, warning and error share one line and swap in
  place, out then in.
- **Status mark:** a change is the content swap: the old mark leaves on fast-01,
  then the new one arrives on fast-02. From no status, it arrives at once.
  `statusBeat` plays the mark's icon once as it arrives. A choice is one act,
  not typing, so a status shows at once.
- **Icon hover:** the field is the chevron's icon frame, so the chevron's motion
  plays on the field's hover. It does not turn.
- **List snap in:** the page-drawn list grows from the field's center on its
  near edge, its width from 25% and its height from 75%, over fast-01 on the
  entrance curve.
- **List snap out:** the far edge pulls back to 70% over fast-01 on the
  pull-back curve, and the list is gone on its last frame.
- **List fade:** the list fades up over the entrance's first fast-00 and out
  over the exit's last, linear.

The platform's own list has no motion of ours.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
The outline and the error border change on half of fast-01. The message line and
the status mark change at once. The page-drawn list fades in at its final size
on the reduced clock, and closes at once.

V12/SelectList.title: SelectList
V12/SelectList.summary:
Pick one value from a vertical list of rows. It is the content switcher's
vertical sibling, on the selection kit's track, selector and keyboard model.
Rows are `SelectItem`s, with an optional icon, secondary text and a trailing
accessory; `SelectItemGroup` adds headings and `SelectItemDivider` a line. With
no value, nothing is marked.

sections.title: Motion
sections.text:
- **Glide:** a pick sends the selector from where it is to the new row, on the
  content switcher's timing by travel. Its leading edge runs up to 24px ahead,
  then both edges land together. A new pick mid-glide starts from where the
  selector is.
- **Reach:** a press on another row moves the leading edge a few px toward it
  before the release. Slide to another row to retarget; slide off the list to
  cancel.
- **Drag:** the selector follows the pointer and lands on the nearest row, with
  a 4px squash at the ends.
- **Arrival:** the first pick grows the selector in from the row's center, 4px
  short, over fast-02. Clearing the value shrinks it back and fades it, over
  fast-01. A value already set on mount is placed at once.
- **Hover:** unselected rows take the rollover; a pressed row takes the pressed
  color while held. A motion icon plays on its row's hover.
- **Keyboard:** ↑, ↓, Home, End and typeahead move between rows, skipping
  disabled ones. With `activation="automatic"` they pick; with `manual` they
  move focus and Enter or Space picks.
- **Loading:** placeholder rows stand in the rows' own boxes. The rows take them
  in order as one reflow, and the track's height follows on the same clock.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
No travel: the selector fades in on the new row as it fades out of the old, on
half the clock. There is no reach. The arrival and the clearing fade in place,
on half the clock. The pressed color still shows; the hover's release is at
once. A loading track changes height at once. `reduced` overrides the preference
for the selector and the hover.

V12/SelectionKit.title: SelectionKit
V12/SelectionKit.summary:
What the v12 selection components (content switcher, tabs, select list, menu)
share: the selection engine's hooks, the selector's faces and styles, and
`SelectionPanels`, the content a selection switches. Each component imports
`selection-kit.scss`; the motion comes from the motion package.

sections.title: SelectionPanels
sections.text:
- **Out:** the old content moves 8px the way the selector goes, and fades.
- **In:** once it has gone, the new content follows from 8px behind. Out then
  in, never overlapping.
- **Box:** `fit="content"` (the default) resizes the container to the new panel,
  starting with the in. `fit="largest"` holds the largest panel's size and never
  resizes.
- **Direction:** `travel="with"` follows the selector on screen, right to left
  included; `against` goes the other way.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.text:
A snap: the new panel replaces the old on one frame, with no travel or fade, and
the container resizes at once.
